STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r30.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r30.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r30.claim: The surah closes with devotional practices, including invoking God's Names and listening to Quran recitation.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r30.anchor:
several verses dealing with pious and
devotional practices, including invoking the Names of God and
listening to the recitation of the Quran (vv. 180, 204–5).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.claim: The Prophet is urged to remain steadfast against opponents’ baseless objections and is shown what can help him persevere.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.anchor: At the end, the Prophet (sws) is urged to be steadfast in the wake of the nonsensical statements of his opponents and their baseless objections.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p159.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p159.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p159.claim: Listening attentively and remaining silent is the way to benefit from the Qur’an’s guidance and insight.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p159.anchor: states the way to benefit from the guidance and insight provided by the Qur’ ān.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p159.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p159.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p159.claim: The verse also condemns disbelievers’ noisy response, which reflects ignorance and deprives them of mercy; attentive listening is the right response and brings mercy.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p159.anchor: The correct attitude is totally opposite to it: they should listen intently instead of making noise.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p159.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p159.speaker: some jurists
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p159.claim: Some jurists cite this verse to support reciting Sūrah al-Fātiḥah behind the prayer leader.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p159.anchor: our jurists also presents this verse in support of their view

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.claim: The author says the verse has another context and its wording instead supports reciting al-Fātiḥah in silent prayers, not loud ones.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.anchor: in the loud prayers S ūrah al-Fātiḥah should not be recited while in the silent prayers, it should be recited.

SAMIN-DURR:7:204/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:204/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:204/r1.claim: The pronoun in له refers to the Qurʾan, and the phrase attaches to استمعوا with the sense 'for its sake.'
SAMIN-DURR:7:204/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { له }: متعلق ب استمعوا، على معنى لأجله، والضمير للقرآن

SAMIN-DURR:7:204/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:204/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:7:204/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa also allows له to mean لله, with the pronoun referring to God; the author finds this unlikely.
SAMIN-DURR:7:204/r2.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " يجوز أن يكون بمعنى لله، أي: لأجله

SAMIN-DURR:7:204/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:204/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:7:204/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows an extra lām giving فاستمعوه; most grammarians permit this only with an advanced object or a derived governing form.
SAMIN-DURR:7:204/r3.anchor: وجوز أيضا أن تكون اللام زائدة، أي: فاستمعوه، وقد عرفت أن هذا لا يجوز عند الجمهور

SAMIN-DURR:7:204/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:204/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:7:204/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa also allows the lām to mean إلى, but the author sees no need for that reading.
SAMIN-DURR:7:204/r4.anchor: وجوز أيضا أن تكون بمعنى إلى ولا حاجة إليه

ZAJJAJ:v2p397/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p397/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p397/r7.claim: A report says conversation in prayer was once allowed, including asking how many units had been prayed; after this verse it was prohibited except for devotional remembrance and requests for pardon.
ZAJJAJ:v2p397/r7.anchor: يروى أن الكلام في الصلاة كان جائزا، فكان يدخل الرجل فيقول:

ZAJJAJ:v2p397/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p397/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p397/r8.claim: The reported prohibition exempts speech that draws near to God, such as glorification, profession of divine unity, magnification, and seeking forgiveness.
ZAJJAJ:v2p397/r8.anchor: التسبيح والتهليل والتكبير والاستغفار وما أشبه ذلك

ZAJJAJ:v2p397/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p397/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p397/r9.claim: Another possible sense is to act according to the Quran and not go beyond it; hearing God's prayer means that He answers it, since He hears and knows.
ZAJJAJ:v2p397/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا، اعملوا بما فيه ولا تجاوزوا

QIRAAT-ER:7:204:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:204:3#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:7:204:3#1/r1.claim: The hamza in quriʾa is softened to yāʾ, a dialectal phonological variant without semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:7:204:3#1/r1.anchor: Hamza replacement: the hamza in quriʾa is softened to yāʾ — a phonological variant

QIRAAT-ER:7:204:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:204:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:7:204:4#1/r1.claim: Dropping the hamza between rāʾ and alif yields Qurān without the glottal stop, a canonical continuous-pronunciation variant.
QIRAAT-ER:7:204:4#1/r1.anchor: Hamza omission: the hamza between rāʾ and alif is dropped, yielding Qurān without glottal stop

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p247/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p247/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p247/r2.claim: Jabir b. ʿAbd Allah says listening in silence is obligatory in two settings: prayer and Friday worship.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p247/r2.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال وجب الإنصات في اثنتين في الصلاة ويوم الجمعة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p247#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p247#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p247#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says this command concerns listening during prayer.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p247#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قال هذا في الصلاة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له ﴾

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p247#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p247#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p247#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says there is no objection to speaking when someone recites outside prayer.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p247#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد قال لا بأس إذا قرأ الرجل في غير صلاة أن يتكلم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p247#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p247#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p247#2/r3.claim: Mujahid disapproves of people behind the imam speaking when the imam recites a verse of warning or mercy, and says they should remain silent.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p247#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه كره إذا مر الإمام بآية خوف أو آية رحمة أن يقول أحد ممن خلفه شيئا قال السكوت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r2.claim: When Quran recitation begins, listeners are to attend and be silent; inṣāt means silence with attentive listening, so they can gain insight, guidance, and mercy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r2.anchor: أمر باستماعه إذا شرع في قراءته وبالإنصات وهو السكوت مع الإصغاء إليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو هريرة وجابر وعطاء وابن المسيب والزهري وعبيد الله بن عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r3.claim: These authorities say the verse answered polytheists who, when the Messenger prayed, told one another not to listen to the Quran and to drown it out.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r3.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود وأبو هريرة وجابر وعطاء وابن المسيب والزهري وعبيد الله بن عمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r4.speaker: عطاء وابن جبير ومجاهد وعمرو بن دينار وزيد بن أسلم والقاسم بن مخيمرة ومسلم بن يسار وشهر بن حوشب وعبد الله بن المبارك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r4.claim: A second group places the command in the Friday sermon; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this because little Quran is recited in sermons and the verse is Meccan, before sermons began after the Hijra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r4.anchor: وقال عطاء أيضا وابن جبير ومجاهد وعمرو بن دينار وزيد بن أسلم والقاسم بن مخيمرة ومسلم بن يسار وشهر بن حوشب وعبد الله بن المبارك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r5.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r5.claim: Ibn Jubayr also applies the command to listening at the two Eid prayers, Friday prayer, and prayers in which the imam recites aloud.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r5.anchor: وقال ابن جبير إنها في الإنصات يوم الأضحى ويوم الفطر ويوم الجمعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the verse ordered silence during prayer, where companions had been greeting one another and speaking about their needs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r6.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود أيضا: كان يسلم بعضنا على بعض في الصلاة ويكلمه في حاجته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says it concerned obligatory prayer: the companions raised their voices while the Quran was read and confused the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: قرأ في الصلاة المكتوبة وقرأ الصحابة رافعي أصواتهم فخلطوا عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r8.claim: Another view makes this a command to listen and be silent when revelation is delivered.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r8.anchor: وقيل: هو أمر بالاستماع والإنصات إذا أدى الوحي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r9.speaker: الزجاج وجماعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r9.claim: Al-Zajjāj and others say the command is not limited to prayer or another setting: it means to act on the Quran and not transgress its teaching, as hearing a prayer can mean answering it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r9.anchor: وقال جماعة منهم الزجاج: ليس المراد الصلاة ولا غيرها وإنما المراد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r10.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes the verse universally: whenever the Quran is recited, every person present must listen and remain silent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r10.anchor: وقال الحسن: هي على عمومها ففي أي موضع قرىء القرآن وجب على كل حاضر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r11.claim: For disbelievers, mercy is hoped for through listening that leads to faith; for believers it is reward for listening, silence, and acting. A universal address gives each group fitting mercy; laʿalla may express hope or purpose.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p261/r11.anchor: فرحمتهم هو ثوابهم على الاستماع والإنصات والعمل بمقتضاه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r1.claim: The command directs people to the means of attaining the Quran’s great benefits.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r1.anchor: إرشاد إلى طريق الفوز بما أشير إليه من المنافع الجليلة التي ينطوي عليها القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r2.claim: The لام may indicate purpose, mean إلى, or be extra, yielding فاستمعوه.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r2.anchor: واللام جوز أن تكون أجلية وأن تكون بمعنى إلى وأن تكون صلة أي فاستمعوه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r3.claim: إنصات is silence; the related forms mean to be silent, listen silently, or make someone silent, and the verbal noun is النصتة.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r3.anchor: والإنصات السكوت يقال : نصت ينصت وأنصت

ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r4.claim: Conjoining silence to listening emphasizes care for the Quran; the purpose is attaining mercy, the highest fruit of its benefits.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r5.claim: Abu Hanifa uses the verse to require a congregant to listen rather than recite behind the imam in both silent and audible prayers: the command covers Quran recited in prayer and elsewhere, and the non-prayer case has separate permission to listen or not.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r5.anchor: والآية دليل لأبي حنيفة رضي الله تعالى عنه في أن المأموم لا يقرأ

ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r6.claim: Mujahid reports that an Ansari man recited behind the Prophet during prayer and this verse was revealed; no grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد قال : قرأ رجل من الأنصار خلف رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r7.claim: Ibn Masud heard people reciting behind him in prayer, rebuked them after it, and quoted God’s command to listen and be silent.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنه صلى بأصحابه فسمع أناسا يقرؤن خلفه فلما انصرف

ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r8.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r8.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit says there is no recitation behind the imam.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r8.anchor: عن زيد بن ثابت قال : لا قراءة خلف الإمام

ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r9.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits the Prophet’s instruction that the imam is followed: when he recites, the congregation should remain silent.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r9.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم إنما جعل الإمام

ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r10.speaker: جابر
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r10.claim: Jabir transmits the Prophetic rule that one praying behind an imam has the imam’s recitation as his own; its transmission and grading are debated in the continuation.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r10.anchor: عن جابر أن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال : من كان له إمام فقراءته له قراءة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r11.claim: If sound, the imam report specifies the general command to recite what is easy and the rule that prayer requires recitation; it can also be specified after the agreed exception for one who catches the imam bowing.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r11.anchor: فجاز التخصيص بعده بالمقتدي بالحديث المذكور

ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r12.claim: The imperative for the person who errs in prayer to recite is read as applying outside following an imam; otherwise the imam’s recitation counts for him and he would have two readings in one prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r12.anchor: فإن قراءة الإمام قراءة له فلو قرأ لكان له قراءتان

ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r13.claim: Although many routes raise Jabir’s report to the Prophet, critics who weaken its raised form concede that the sounder transmission is mursal through Musa ibn Abi Aisha and Abdullah ibn Shaddad; Abu Hanifa also transmitted it mursal.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r13.anchor: بأن الصحيح أنه مرسل لأن الحفاظ كالسفيانيين وأبي الأحوص وشعبة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r14.claim: Alusi answers that the mursal report is authoritative for most scholars and sufficient for his school’s ruling and its dialectical case; even if set aside, Abu Hanifa raised it through a sound chain.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p150#2/r14.anchor: المرسل حجة عند أكثر أهل العلم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r1.speaker: محمد بن الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r1.claim: In his Muwatta, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan transmits through Abu Hanifa, Musa ibn Abi Aisha, Abdullah ibn Shaddad, and Jabir the Prophet’s ruling that the imam’s recitation counts for the follower.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r1.anchor: وروى محمد بن الحسن في موطئه قال : أنبأنا أبو حنيفة حدثنا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r2.speaker: أحمد بن منيع
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r2.claim: Ahmad ibn Maniʿ’s Musnad raises the report through Sufyan and Sharik from Jabir; it also gives Jarir’s version ending at the Prophet without Jabir.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r2.anchor: قال أحمد بن منيع في مسنده : أخبرنا إسحق الأزرق حدثنا سفيان

ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r3.speaker: عبد بن حميد
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r3.claim: Abd ibn Humayd transmits the raised Jabir report through Abu Nuaym, Hasan ibn Salih, and Abu al-Zubayr; Alusi says the first Jabir chain meets the two Ṣaḥīḥs’ standard and the second Muslim’s.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r3.anchor: ورواه عبد بن حميد قال : حدثنا أبو نعيم حدثنا الحسن بن صالح

ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r4.claim: Alusi rejects the claim that the named hadith masters did not raise the report: Sufyan, Sharik, Jarir, and Abu al-Zubayr did so through sound routes.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r4.anchor: أبو الزبير ورفعوه بالطرق الصحيحة فبطل عدهم فيمن لم يرفعه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r5.claim: Even a reliable narrator’s solitary raising would be accepted as an addition by a trustworthy transmitter; here he is not alone, and a transmitter may sometimes connect a report and sometimes transmit it mursal.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r5.anchor: ولو تفرد الثقة وجب قبوله لأن الرفع زيادة وزيادة الثقة مقبولة فكيف ولم ينفرد

ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة والحاكم
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r6.claim: A report in Abu Hanifa’s biography, also given by al-Hakim, recounts that a man recited behind the Prophet, a companion forbade him, and the Prophet ruled that the imam’s recitation counts for the follower.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r6.anchor: وذكر فيها قصة وبها أخرجه أبو عبدالله الحاكم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r7.claim: Abu Hanifa’s version locates the incident in the noon or afternoon prayer and says a companion gestured to stop a man reciting behind the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r7.anchor: وفي رواية لأبي حنيفة إن ذلك كان في الظهر أو العصر وهي أن رجلا قرأ خلف رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r8.claim: Jabir sometimes reports only the legal ruling and sometimes the full incident; because the story supports the companion’s prohibition, especially in a silent prayer, it bars recitation rather than permitting choice.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p151/r8.anchor: إن جابرا روى منه محل الحكم فقط تارة والمجموع تارة ويتضمن رد القراءة خلف الإمام

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r1.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r1.claim: Ubadah ibn al-Samit reports that after the Prophet’s heavy recitation in dawn prayer, he asked whether they recited behind him; he forbade it except for the Opening of the Book, without which prayer is invalid.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r1.anchor: وكذا ما رواه أبو داود والترمذي عن عبادة بن الصامت قال : كنا خلف رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r2.claim: Where the reports conflict, Alusi gives priority to the unrestricted prohibition because it came later and has the stronger chain.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r2.anchor: ويقدم لتقدم المنع على الإطلاق عند التعارض ولقوة السند فإن حديث المنع أصح

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r3.claim: He rejects partisan criticism of Abu Hanifa’s report method: the Imam required a narrator to recall a report before accepting it even when he recognized his own handwriting, stricter than hadith masters.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r3.anchor: مع تضييقه في الرواية إلى الغاية حتى أنه شرط التذكر لجوازها بعد علم الراوي أن ذلك المروي خطه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r4.claim: Other Jabir reports, though weak, and the reported practice of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Zayd ibn Thabit, and Ibn Masud support the prohibition.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r4.anchor: وإن ضعفت وبمذاهب الصحابة أيضا كابن عباس وابن عمر وزيد بن ثابت وابن مسعود

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r5.speaker: عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r5.claim: Through Muhammad from Dawud ibn Qays, Umar wishes that a stone were in the mouth of whoever recites behind the imam.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r5.anchor: عن داود بن قيس بن عجلان أن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : ليت في فم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r6.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r6.claim: A similar statement forbidding recitation behind the imam is also reported from Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r6.anchor: وروي مثل ذلك عن سعد بن أبي وقاص

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r7.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r7.claim: Ali is reported to say that whoever recites behind the imam has erred in the fitra, though Alusi notes a criticism in its transmission.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r7.anchor: وروي عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه إلا أن فيه مقالا أنه قال : من قرأ

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r8.speaker: الشعبي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r8.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says he met seventy veterans of Badr, all of whom forbade a congregant from reciting behind the imam.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r8.anchor: وقال الشعبي : أدركت سبعين بدريا كلهم يمنعون المقتدي

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r9.speaker: بعض أصحابنا
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r9.claim: Some Hanafis claim the Companions unanimously forbade follower recitation; Alusi says this may mean many leading Companions, since literal or tacit consensus is doubtful.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r9.anchor: وقد ادعى بعض أصحابنا إجماع الصحابة رضي الله تعالى عنهم على ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r10.speaker: عروة بن الزبير والقاسم بن محمد والزهري ومالك وابن المبارك وأحمد وإسحق
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r10.claim: Another group, also reported from Ibn Umar, says the follower recites when the imam is silent but not when he recites aloud, combining the verse’s listening command with the Sunnah’s alleged duty to recite.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r10.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أن المأموم يقرأ إذا أسر الإمام القراءة ولا يقرأ إذا جهر وهو قول عروة بن الزبير والقاسم بن محمد

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r11.claim: Alusi objects that a silent follower’s not being called a listener does not establish a Sunnah duty to recite; the proof is difficult, and one should follow the stronger evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r11.anchor: واعترض بأنه وإن سلمنا أنه لا يقال له منصت مع علمه بالقراءة وبأنا لا نسلم دلالة السنة على وجوب القراءة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r12.claim: Alusi doubts the report that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan recommended al-Fatiha as a precaution, saying his actual ruling matches Abu Hanifa and Abu Yusuf in disliking follower recitation under the warning.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152/r12.anchor: ومن هنا ضعف ما يروى عن محمد بن الحسن رحمه الله تعالى أنه يستحسن قراءة الفاتحة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r1.speaker: محمد بن الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r1.claim: In Kitab al-Athar, Muhammad cites Alqama ibn Qays as never reciting behind an imam in either kind of prayer and says this is the rule they follow; his Muwatta gives the same position.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r1.anchor: قال في كتاب الآثار بعد ما أسند إلى علقمة بن قيس : إنه ما قرأ قط

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r2.speaker: السرخسي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r2.claim: Al-Sarakhsi says recitation behind the imam invalidates prayer according to several Companions, reportedly including Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r2.anchor: وقال السرخسي تفسد صلاة القاريء خلف الإمام

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r3.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r3.claim: The Muzani transmission from al-Shafiʿi has the follower recite in both audible and silent prayers; the Buwaiti transmission has al-Fatiha and a surah in silent prayer, and al-Fatiha alone in audible prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r3.anchor: وفي رواية المزني عن الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه يقرأ في الجهرية والسرية

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r4.speaker: الشافعية
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r4.claim: The prevalent Shafiʿi view is that a follower who hears the imam in an audible prayer listens without reciting; if he cannot distinguish the words or the prayer is silent, he recites according to the relied-on view.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r4.anchor: والمشهور عند الشافعية أنه لا سورة للمأموم الذي يسمع الإمام في جهرية بل يستمع فإن بعد بأن لم يسمع

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra says people used to speak during prayer and this verse was revealed; Alusi distinguishes this occasion from the report about recitation behind the imam.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r5.anchor: فقد روى أبو هريرة رضي الله تعالى عنه أنهم كانوا يتكلمون في الصلاة فنزلت

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r6.claim: Some understand القرآن here as the Friday sermon and take listening as obligatory or recommended; Hanafis hold silence during the sermon obligatory, with qualifications.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r6.anchor: ومن الناس من فسر القرآن بالخطبة والأمر بالإستماع أما للوجوب أو الندب وعندنا الإنصات في الخطبة فرض

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r7.claim: Mujahid says the verse applies to prayer and the Friday sermon.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r7.anchor: وأخرج غير واحد عن مجاهد رضي الله تعالى عنه أن الآية في الصلاة والخطبة يوم الجمعة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r8.claim: Hanafi texts indicate a general duty to listen whenever Quran is recited aloud: the Khulasa assigns sin to a reader whose nearby listener cannot attend, including loud night recitation while people sleep.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r8.anchor: قال في الخلاصة : رجل يكتب الفقه وبجنبه رجل يقرأ القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r9.claim: The obligation applies by the wording’s general scope, not just its occasion; إذا expresses universality here, as in most Quranic conditional clauses using it.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r9.anchor: بأن العبرة بعموم اللفظ لا بخصوص السبب و ( إذا ) هنا للكلية

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r10.claim: The apparent sense of استماع is listening; al-Zajjaj instead figuratively takes it as acceptance and response, as in familiar devotional and royal expressions.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r10.anchor: والمراد من الإستماع في الآية المعنى المتبادر منه وقال الزجاج : المراد منه القبول

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r11.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r11.claim: Al-Tibi prefers acceptance and response because it coheres with the preceding and following discourse and gathers the interpretations: believers must accept, act on, and adhere to the Quran.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r11.anchor: ورجح ذلك العلامة الطيبي قال : وهذا أوفق لتأليف النظم الكريم سابقا ولاحقا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r12.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r12.claim: The context contrasts unbelievers who scorn and reject the Quran with believers instructed to do more than hear: accept it, act by it, and adhere to it for mercy; naming the Quran instead of using a pronoun emphasizes its causal force.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r12.anchor: لما ذكر تعريضا أن المشركين إنما استهزأوا بالقرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r13.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r13.claim: On al-Tibi’s interpretation, silence in prayer is required a fortiori because prayer is intimate conversation; the command also covers listening when the Prophet recites.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r13.anchor: ويدخل في هذا وجوب الإنصات في الصلاة بطريق الأولى لأنها مقام المناجاة والإستماع من المتكلم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r14.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r14.claim: This contextual reading makes the addressees believers; al-Tibi says that is explicit in the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r14.anchor: ويعلم منه أن الخطاب في الآية للمؤمنين بل هو نص في ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r15.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r15.claim: Another view addresses unbelievers: if they listen to the Quran at its revelation, they can recognize its inimitability and need no further signs.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r15.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إن الخطاب فيها للكفار وذلك أن كون القرآن بصائر وهدى ورحمة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r16.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r16.claim: Supporters of an unbelieving audience say the hope of mercy suits them, unlike believers already assured of mercy in Quran 45:20.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r16.anchor: في آخر الآية ( لعلكم ترحمون ) بناء على أن ذلك للترجي

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r17.claim: Alusi answers that the hoped-for mercy may differ from the mercy already stated; even if identical, a generous giver may properly keep hope alive.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r17.anchor: وأجيب بأن هذه الرحمة المرجوة غير تلك الرحمة ولئن سلم كونها إياها فالأطماع من الكريم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r18.claim: The passive construction indicates that the reader may be anyone.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r18.anchor: وفي بناء الفعل للمفعول إشارة إلى أن مدار القراءة من أي قاريء كان

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r19.claim: Some companions recommend honoring Quran recitation outside prayer by wearing one’s best clothes and a turban and facing the qibla; knowledge receives similar honor.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r19.anchor: قال بعض الأصحاب : يستحب لمريد قراءته خارج الصلاة أن يلبس أحسن ثيابه ويتعمم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r20.claim: Reciting while reclining is unobjectionable as remembrance, since God praises those who remember standing, sitting, and lying on their sides.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r20.anchor: ولو قرأ مضطجعا فلا بأس إذ هو نوع من الذكر وقد مدح سبحانه ذاكريه قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r21.claim: During recitation one should draw in the legs rather than stretch them, which is poor etiquette; walking or working is acceptable if the heart remains attentive, otherwise it is disliked.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r21.anchor: ويضم رجليه عند القراءة ولا يمدها لأنه سوء أدب ولو قرأ ماشيا أو عند النسج ونحوه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r22.claim: One should not recite with uncovered private parts or in the presence of an uncovered person, even one’s wife; some also dislike reciting in bathhouses and roads.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r22.anchor: ولا يقرأ وهو مكشوف العورة أو كان بحضرته من هو كذلك وإن كانت زوجته وكره بعضهم القراءة في الحمام والطريق

ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r23.speaker: النووي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r23.claim: Al-Nawawi says the Shafiʿi school does not dislike recitation in bathhouses or roads but does dislike it in a toilet and a mill house while its wheel turns; Alusi says this matches the Hanafi school.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p152#2/r23.anchor: قال النووي : ومذهبنا لا تكره فيهما وتكره في الحش وبيت الرحى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r8.claim: A group says the verse was revealed about recitation in prayer; Abū Hurayra reports that worshippers spoke about their needs during prayer and were told to be quiet and listen.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r8.anchor: فذهب جماعة إلى أنها في القراءة في الصلاة، روي عن أبي هريرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r9.claim: Another group says the verse requires not reciting aloud behind the imam.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r9.anchor: وقال قوم: نزلت في ترك الجهر بالقراءة خلف الإمام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r10.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the verse concerned people raising their voices while praying behind the Messenger of God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r10.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: نزلت هذه الآية في رفع الأصوات وهم خلف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الصلاة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r11.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r11.claim: Al-Kalbī says they raised their voices in prayer when they heard mention of Paradise and Hell.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r11.anchor: وقال الكلبي: كانوا يرفعون أصواتهم في الصلاة حين يسمعون ذكر الجنة والنار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r12.claim: Ibn Masʿūd rebuked people for reciting along with the imam and invoked this command to listen and be quiet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r12.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أنه سمع ناسا يقرأون مع الإمام فلما انصرف قال: أما آن لكم أن تفقهوا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r13.speaker: الحسن والزهري والنخعي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r13.claim: Al-Ḥasan, al-Zuhrī, and al-Nakhaʿī hold that the verse concerns listening during prayer recitation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r13.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن والزهري والنخعي: أن الآية في القراءة في الصلاة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r14.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وعطاء ومجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r14.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿAṭāʾ, and Mujāhid say the verse concerns listening to the imam's Friday sermon.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r14.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير وعطاء ومجاهد: إن الآية في الخطبة، أمروا بالإنصات لخطبة الإمام يوم الجمعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r15.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r15.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr extends the command to the sermons on Eid al-Aḍḥā, Eid al-Fiṭr, and Friday, and to what the imam recites aloud.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r15.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: هذا في الإنصات يوم الأضحى والفطر ويوم الجمعة، وفيما يجهر به الإمام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r16.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318#3/r16.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz says one must listen quietly to every preacher.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:204/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:204/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:204/r1.claim: The verse was revealed when people spoke during prayer; they were ordered to listen to the imam's recitation and remain silent.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:204/r1.anchor: نزلت في الصلاة كانوا يتكلمون فيها فأمروا باستماع قراءة الإمام والإنصات له

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:204/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:204/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:204/r2.claim: The apparent wording requires listening and silence whenever the Qur'an is recited, without restriction to prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:204/r2.anchor: وظاهر اللفظ يقتضي وجوبهما حيث يقرأ القرآن مطلقا

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:204/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:204/r3.speaker: عامة العلماء
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:204/r3.claim: The majority of scholars consider listening and silence recommended outside prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:204/r3.anchor: وعامة العلماء على استحبابهما خارج الصلاة

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:204/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:204/r4.speaker: من لا يرى وجوب القراءة على المأموم
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:204/r4.claim: Those who infer that the follower in prayer is not obliged to recite rely on this verse, but al-Bayḍāwī calls the argument weak.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:204/r4.anchor: واحتج به من لا يرى وجوب القراءة على المأموم وهو ضعيف

BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r7.claim: The recited Qur'an is the revelation just described and the attribute of their Lord, so listeners should approach it humbly and with proper courtesy.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r8.claim: Listening requires directing one's ears to the recitation and making an effort to avoid distractions.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r8.anchor: ألقوا إليه أسماعكم مجتهدين في عدم شاغل يشغلكم عن السمع

BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r9.claim: The verse's apparent ruling requires everyone to be silent for every reciter; Biqaʿi urges silence because the Qur'an merits undivided attention.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r9.anchor: ظاهر الآية وجوب الإنصات لكل قارئ على كل أحد

BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r10.claim: Silence enables reflection and deliberation, unveiling the heart so listeners understand and act on the Qur'an without inward resistance.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r10.anchor: للتأمل والتدبر لتنجلي قلوبكم فتعلموا حقيقة فتعلموا بما فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r11.claim: The command offers hope that God will honor the listeners as a merciful person treats the recipient of mercy.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r11.anchor: لتكون على رجاء من أن يكرمكم ربكم ويفعل بكم كل ما يفعله الراحم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r12.claim: The command moves from remembering God at Satan's prompting to listening to the Qur'an, the greatest remembrance, and applies reading etiquette in every situation.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r12.anchor: ولما تقدم الأمر بالذكر عند نزغ الشيطان

BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r13.claim: The reciter may raise his voice to gain listeners or recite quietly to avoid obliging others to listen; the command covers both cases.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r13.anchor: وربما أسر لئلا يوجب على غيره الإصغاء

BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r14.claim: The address shifts from the audience to their leader, the Prophet, to encourage their acceptance and suggest that he alone can fully carry out this duty.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p177/r14.anchor: ورقي الخطاب منهم إلى إمامهم ليكون أدعى لقبولهم

BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r1.claim: Listening means receptive attention and acting on the Qur’an; its majesty calls for listening generally, and intentional listening involves effort and purpose.
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r1.anchor: {وإذا قرىء القرءان} الذي ذكرت شؤونه العظيمة. {فاستمعوا له} استماع قبول وعمل بما فيه فإن شأنه يوجب الاستماع مطلقا

BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r2.claim: A listener is someone who deliberately attends, while a hearer may hear by chance; every listener hears, but not everyone who hears is a listener.
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r2.anchor: فرقوا بين المستمع والسامع بأن المستمع من كان قاصدا للسماع مصغيا إليه والسامع من اتفق سماعه من غير قصد إليه

BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r3.claim: Inṣāt is silence throughout recitation while attending to it, honoring and completing the act of listening; unlike mere silence, it entails listening.
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r3.anchor: {وأنصتوا} أي : واسكتوا في خلال القراءة وراعوها إلى انقضائها تعظيما له وتكميلا للاستماع والفرق بين الإنصات والسكوت أن الإنصات مأخوذ في مفهومه الاستماع

BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r4.claim: The hoped-for mercy is the greatest fruit of listening to the Qur’an.
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r4.anchor: {لعلكم ترحمون} أي : تفوزون بالرحمة التي هي أقصى ثمراته.

BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says Muslims previously talked and managed needs during prayer, even asking and answering how many units remained; the verse then ordered silence during recitation, the prayer’s greatest pillar.
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : كان المسلمون قبل نزول هذه الآية يتكلمون في الصلاة ويأمرون بحوائجهم

BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r6.claim: Abu Hanifa infers that a congregant must listen and that the imam’s recitation counts for the follower, who should not recite behind him whether recitation is quiet or audible.
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r6.anchor: استدل الإمام أبو حنيفة بهذه الآية على أن إنصات المقتدي واجب وأن قراءة الإمام قراءة المأموم فلا يقرأ خلف الإمام

BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r7.claim: His argument is that God commands both listening and silence; when listening is inapplicable, silence remains obligatory, and general wording applies beyond the specific occasion.
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r7.anchor: وجه الاستدلال أن المراد بالإنصات المأمور به وإن كان هو النهي عن الكلام لا عن القراءة لكن العبرة لعموم اللفظ لا لخصوص السبب

BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r8.speaker: الحدادي
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r8.claim: Some exegetes say the verse was revealed specifically about prayer when people recited behind the Prophet; al-Haddadi considers this the soundest view.
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r8.anchor: على أن جماعة من المفسرين قالوا إن الآية نزلت في الصلاة خاصة حين كانوا يقرؤون القرآن خلفه عليه السلام وجعله الحدادي في "تفسيره" أصح.

BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r9.claim: Al-Ashbah says Abu Hanifa forbade follower recitation to prevent confusion for the imam; Ibn Malik’s commentary identifies it as prohibitively disliked.
BURSEVI:v3p231#2/r9.anchor: قال في "الأشباه" أسقط أبو حنيفة القراءة عن المأموم بل منعه منها شفعة على الإمام دفعا للتخليط عليه

BURSEVI:v3p233/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p233/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p233/r1.claim: Inṣāt enables good listening, which enables divine audition: silence with the outer tongue and ears, then with the inner tongue and ears, brings mercy through true hearing.
BURSEVI:v3p233/r1.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : الإنصات شرط في حسن الاستماع وحسن الإستماع شرط في الإسماع

BURSEVI:v3p233/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p233/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p233/r2.claim: True hearing is described as God becoming the servant’s hearing; hearing the Qur’an through its Creator means truly hearing it from its reciter, linked to 55:1–2.
BURSEVI:v3p233/r2.anchor: لعلكم ترحمون} بالاستماع بالسمع الحقيقي وهو قوله : "كنت له سمعا فبي يسمع" فمن سمع القرآن بسمع بارئه فقد سمع من قارئه

BURSEVI:v3p233/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p233/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p233/r3.claim: The inward account links listening to the Qur’an with “The Merciful taught the Qur’an.”

BURSEVI:v3p233/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p233/r4.speaker: المولى الجامي
BURSEVI:v3p233/r4.claim: The quoted Persian couplet says a blind bat sees only a speck of sunlight, as a limited reader takes only letters from the Qur’an.
BURSEVI:v3p233/r4.anchor: قال المولى الجامي مربنده سنائي غزنوى است :

DURR-FULL:v3p633/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p633/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v3p633/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the verse was revealed because people behind the Prophet raised their voices during prayer.
DURR-FULL:v3p633/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة في قوله {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} قال: نزلت في رفع الأصوات

DURR-FULL:v3p633/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p633/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p633/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the command applies in the obligatory prayer.
DURR-FULL:v3p633/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} يعني في الصلاة المفروضة

DURR-FULL:v3p633/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p633/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p633/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the verse came down after people recited behind the Prophet in prayer.
DURR-FULL:v3p633/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: صلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقرأ خلفه قوم فنزلت {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا}

DURR-FULL:v3p633/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p633/r8.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
DURR-FULL:v3p633/r8.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi says people used to answer the Prophet’s recitation in prayer, repeating his words from the basmala through the sura; after the command came, they fell silent and the Prophet recited.
DURR-FULL:v3p633/r8.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قرأ في الصلاة أجابه من وراءه

DURR-FULL:v3p634/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r1.claim: Mujahid says an Ansari man recited behind the Prophet in prayer, and the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: قرأرجل من الأنصار

DURR-FULL:v3p634/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مغفل
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r2.claim: Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal says the rule is not for everyone hearing Qur’an, but applies when an imam recites.
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مغفل أنه سئل أكل من سمع القرآن يقرأ وجب عليه الاستماع والإنصات قال: لا

DURR-FULL:v3p634/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r3.claim: Ibn Masud rebuked companions he heard reciting behind him in prayer and reminded them God commanded listening and silence.
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنه صلى بأصحابه فسمع ناسا يقرؤون خلفه فلما انصرف قال: أما آن لكم أن تفهموا

DURR-FULL:v3p634/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r4.claim: Ibn Masud says the worshipper should be silent when the imam recites; prayer occupies one, and the imam’s recitation suffices.
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r4.anchor: عن أبي وائل عن ابن مسعود أنه قال في القراءة خلف الإمام:

DURR-FULL:v3p634/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r5.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r5.claim: Ali says reciting behind the imam errs from the proper natural practice.
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r5.anchor: عن علي قال: من قرأ خلف الإمام فقد أخطأ الفطرة

DURR-FULL:v3p634/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r6.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit says there is no recitation behind the imam.
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r6.anchor: عن زيد بن ثابت قال: لا قراءة خلف الإمام

DURR-FULL:v3p634/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r7.claim: The Prophet says the imam is appointed to be followed; when he recites, the congregation should be silent.
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما جعل الإمام ليؤتم به

DURR-FULL:v3p634/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r8.claim: The Prophet says whoever has an imam has the imam’s recitation as his own.
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r8.anchor: عن جابر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: من كان له إمام

DURR-FULL:v3p634/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r9.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r9.claim: Ibrahim says reciting behind the imam was a later innovation; people had not done so at first.
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r9.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال: أول ما أحدثوا القراءة

DURR-FULL:v3p634/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r10.speaker: الزهري
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r10.claim: Al-Zuhri says the verse was revealed about an Ansari youth who repeated what the Prophet recited.
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r10.anchor: عن الزهري قال: نزلت هذه الآية في فتى من الأنصار

DURR-FULL:v3p634/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r11.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r11.claim: Abu al-Aliyah says the Companions recited behind the Prophet in prayer; after the verse came down they fell silent.
DURR-FULL:v3p634/r11.anchor: عن أبي العالية أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا صلى بأصحابه فقرأ

DURR-FULL:v3p635/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r1.claim: Ibn Umar says Israelites answered their leaders’ recitation, which God disapproved for this community, commanding it to listen silently.
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: كانت بنو إسرائيل إذا قرأت أئمتهم جاوبوهم

DURR-FULL:v3p635/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r2.claim: Ibrahim says the verse came down while the Prophet and another man were both reciting.
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r2.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ ورجل يقرأ

DURR-FULL:v3p635/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r3.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r3.claim: Talha ibn Musarrif says the reciters meant here are not the imams Muslims were commanded to listen to.
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r3.anchor: عن طلحة بن مصرف في قوله {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} قال: ليس هؤلاء بالأئمة

DURR-FULL:v3p635/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra says the verse was revealed after people spoke during prayer.
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r4.anchor: من طريق أبي هريرة قال: كانوا يتكلمون في الصلاة فنزلت

DURR-FULL:v3p635/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r5.claim: Ibn Masud greeted the Prophet during prayer and received no answer; afterward the Prophet said God does as He wills, and the verse was revealed. Speech had previously occurred in prayer.
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنه سلم على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصلي فلم يرد عليه

DURR-FULL:v3p635/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r6.claim: Ibn Masud says they greeted one another during prayer until the Qur’an commanded listening and silence.
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r6.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: كنا يسلم بعضنا على بعض في الصلاة فجاء القرآن

DURR-FULL:v3p635/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن مغفل
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r7.claim: Ibn Mughaffal says people used to speak in prayer; this verse came down and the Prophet forbade speech there.
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r7.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مغفل قال: كان الناس يتكلمون في الصلاة فأنزل الله هذه الآية

DURR-FULL:v3p635/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r8.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r8.claim: Ata says Muslims talked in prayer like Jews and Christians until this verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r8.anchor: عن عطاء قال: بلغني أن المسلمين كانوا يتكلمون في الصلاة

DURR-FULL:v3p635/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r9.claim: Qatada says early worshippers talked during prayer, even asking how many units had been performed. Silence lets the worshipper hear, understand, and retain recitation; silence is with the tongue, listening with the ears.
DURR-FULL:v3p635/r9.anchor: عن قتادة قال: كانوا يتكلمون في الصلاة أول ما أمروا بها

DURR-FULL:v3p636/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r1.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak says people used to talk in prayer and this verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك قال: كانوا يتكلمون في الصلاة فأنزل الله

DURR-FULL:v3p636/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas applies the command to Friday prayer, the two Eids, and audible Qur’an recitation in prayer.
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له}

DURR-FULL:v3p636/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says believers generally have latitude in listening, except during Friday, Eid, and loud recitation in prayer.
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: المؤمن في سعة من الاستماع إليه

DURR-FULL:v3p636/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas applies it to raised voices behind the Prophet in prayer and the Friday sermon, which he considers prayer; he says speaking during the sermon nullifies prayer.
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} قال: نزلت في رفع الأصوات

DURR-FULL:v3p636/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r5.claim: Mujahid says the command applies during prayer and the Friday sermon.
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد في هذه الآية {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} قال: هذا في الصلاة

DURR-FULL:v3p636/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r6.claim: Mujahid says silence is obligatory when the imam recites in prayer and when he preaches on Friday.
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: وجب الإنصات في اثنتين في الصلاة والإمام يقرأ

DURR-FULL:v3p636/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r7.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r7.claim: Ata grounds Friday listening in this verse and says the rule is the same as listening in prayer.
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r7.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال: قلت لعطاء:

DURR-FULL:v3p636/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r8.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says the command applies during prescribed prayer and remembrance.
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r8.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} قال: عند الصلاة المكتوبة

DURR-FULL:v3p636/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r9.speaker: الكلبي
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r9.claim: Al-Kalbi says people raised their voices in prayer when hearing mention of Paradise and Hell, prompting revelation.
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r9.anchor: عن الكلبي قال: كانوا يرفعون أصواتهم في الصلاة حين يسمعون ذكر الجنة

DURR-FULL:v3p636/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says the command applies in prayer and when revelation descends.
DURR-FULL:v3p636/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له} الآية

DURR-FULL:v3p637/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r1.claim: Mujahid disapproved of followers responding to an imam’s verse of warning or mercy; they should remain silent.
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه كره إذا مر الإمام بآية خوف أو آية رحمة

DURR-FULL:v3p637/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r2.speaker: عثمان بن زائدة
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r2.claim: Uthman ibn Zaida covered his face during recitation, avoiding visual or bodily distractions from listening.
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r2.anchor: عن عثمان بن زائدة أنه كان إذا قرىء عليه القرآن غطى وجهه بثوبه

DURR-FULL:v3p637/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r3.claim: The Prophet says listening to one Qur’anic verse earns a doubled good deed and reciting it becomes light on Resurrection; the source grades the report hasan.
DURR-FULL:v3p637/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من استمع إلى آية من كتاب الله

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra says the verse was revealed because people behind the Messenger raised their voices in prayer.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن هذه الاية : واذا قرئ القران فاستمعوا له وانصتوا قال : نزلت في رفع الاصوات

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b says people used to repeat the Prophet's recitation in prayer; after this verse came down, he recited and they listened silently.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظى : قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اذا قرا في الصلاة اجابه من وراءه

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra says people used to speak during prayer, and the verse was revealed about prayer.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r3.anchor: عن ابى عياض عن أبي هريرة قال : كانوا يتكلمون في الصلاة فنزلت : واذا قرئ القران فاستمعوا له

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r4.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports that the Prophet did not answer his greeting during prayer; afterward he said that speaking in prayer had been allowed before this verse descended.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r4.anchor: عن أبي وائل ان ابن مسعود سلم على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم يرد عليه

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r5.speaker: عبد الله
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r5.claim: Abdullah challenges his listeners to understand the Qur'an and invokes the command to listen attentively when it is recited.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله قال : لعلكم تقرون ؟ قلنا : نعم قال : الا تفقهون ؟ مالكم لا تعقلون

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r6.claim: Mujahid says the verse was revealed when a man recited behind the Messenger.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1645/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد قال : قرا رجل خلف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فانزلت واذا قرئ القران

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r1.speaker: معاوية بن قرة المزني
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r1.claim: Mu'awiya ibn Qurra tentatively attributes the verse's occasion to Abdullah ibn Mufaddal and says it concerns listening silently when the imam recites.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r1.anchor: عن معاوية بن قرة المزني قال : احسبه عن عبد الله بن مفضل قال : انما نزلت واذا قرئ القران

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas describes the believer as having latitude concerning listening and names Friday, obligatory prayer, and the two Eids as relevant occasions.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : ان المؤمن في سعة من الاستماع إلى يوم جمعة ، أو في صلاة مكتوبة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r3.claim: Mujahid says silence is obligatory in prayer when the imam recites and during the Friday sermon.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد قال : وجب الانصات في اثنتين من الصلاة والامام يقرا وفي الجمعة والامام يخطب

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r4.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd reports his father as saying that when the verse was revealed, one should be standing in prayer.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r4.anchor: اخبرني ابن زيد ، عن أبيه قال : حين انزلت واذا قرئ القران فاستمعوا له وانصتوا قال : يكون قائما في الصلاة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the command applies in prayer and when revelation is descending from God.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس في قوله : واذا قرئ القران فاستمعوا له وانصتوا لعلكم ترحمون

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says that when one sits with the Qur'an, one should listen to it silently.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1646/r6.anchor: عن الحسن واذا قرئ القران فاستمعوا له وانصتوا قال : اذا جلست إلى القران فانصت له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r1.claim: The conjunction carries the address forward from 7:203: the Messenger is to tell the polytheists, explicitly or implicitly, not to turn away from hearing and considering the Qur'an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r1.anchor: يؤذن العطف بأن الخطاب بالأمر في قوله : { فاستمعوا وأنصتوا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r2.claim: The warning targets polytheists who refused to listen and urged one another to make noise, as described in 41:26; the Qur'an is a great sign, insight, guidance, and mercy for believers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r2.anchor: وقد علم من أحوال المشركين أنهم كانوا يتناهون عن الإنصات إلى القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r3.claim: Naming the Qur'an again instead of using a pronoun honors it, emphasizes the instruction, and lets the sentence stand independently, a recognized eloquent usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r3.anchor: وذكر اسم القرآن إظهار في مقام الإضمار ، لأن القرآن تقدم ذكره بواسطة اسم الإشارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r4.claim: Istima is attentive listening, with its derived form suggesting intensity; insat means listening while stopping speech, adding silence to the command to listen.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r4.anchor: والاستماع الإصغاء وصيغة الافتعال دالة على المبالغة في الفعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r5.claim: Istima may also be figurative for heeding and acting on the Qur'an, as in 7:198; insat then combines attentive listening with abandoning frivolous speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الاستماع مستعملا في معناه المجازي ، وهو الامتثال للعمل بما فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r6.claim: The address includes disbelievers as those being admonished and Muslims as those being guided; believers are especially likely to benefit, following 7:203.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r6.anchor: وهذا الخطاب شامل للكفار على وجه التبليغ ، وللمسلمين على وجه الارشاد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r7.claim: The verse belongs with the preceding Meccan verses whether its direct audience is both groups, Muslims explicitly and polytheists implicitly, or polytheists for guidance and Muslims all the more.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p238#2/r7.anchor: ولا شبهة في أن هذه الآية نزلت في جملة الآيات التي قبلها وعلى مناسبتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r1.claim: Listening and silence should lead to reflection, inference, faith in the Messenger, and reform of the soul through the Qur'an; the command invites proclamation, thought, and action, at levels suited to each hearer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r1.anchor: فالاستماع والإنصات المأمور بهما هما المؤديان بالسامع إلى النظر والاستدلال ، والاهتداء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r2.claim: The command is general in wording only imperfectly: context and the anti-listening response in 41:26 clarify part of its scope, with other cases settled by further evidence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r2.anchor: فهذه الآية مجملة في معنى الاستماع والإنصات وفي مقتضى الأمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r3.claim: Scholars agree the verse's apparent wording is interpreted in many situations; it cannot require every Muslim to stop work and listen whenever anyone recites nearby.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r3.anchor: وقد اتفق علماء الأمة على أن ظاهر الآية بمجرده في صور كثيرة مؤول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r4.claim: A reported interpretation says the verse concerns hearing the imam recite aloud in prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r4.anchor: فرووا عن أبي هريرة أنها نزلت في قراءة الإمام في الجهر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r5.speaker: رجل من الأنصار
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r5.claim: Another report says an Ansari prayed behind the Prophet in an audible prayer and recited while the Prophet recited, prompting the command to listen to the imam.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r5.anchor: أن رجلا من الأنصار صلى وراء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صلاة جهرية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects restricting the command to an imam's recitation: the occasion report is unsound, does not fit the verse's arrangement, and is interpretation rather than a Prophetic transmission.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r6.anchor: وهذا تأويل ضعيف ، لأن نزول الآية على هذا السبب لم يصح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r7.claim: The Maliki tendency is to retain a near-general command but treat it as recommended; Ibn Ashur says it would be better to mean the Messenger's recitation to people so they may know and act on the Qur'an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p239/r7.anchor: ومنهم من أبقى أمر الاستماع على إطلاقه القريب من العموم ، ولكنهم تأولوه على أمر الندب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p240/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p240/r1.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p240/r1.claim: Al-Qurtubi quotes Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: when the polytheists came as the Prophet prayed, they told one another not to listen and to make noise, and this verse answered them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p240/r1.anchor: وفي ( تفسير القرطبي ) عن سعيد ( بن المسيب ) : كان المشركون يأتون رسول الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p240/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p240/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p240/r2.claim: Ibn Ashur says the proposed occasions do not fit: this verse is Meccan, whereas those incidents occurred in Medina.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p240/r2.anchor: على أن ما تقدم من الاخبار في محمل سبب نزول هذه الآية لا يستقيم لأن الآية مكية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p240/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p240/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p240/r3.claim: The verse does not support the Hanafi argument for a follower to omit recitation when the imam recites silently, because that omission is not listening and silence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p240/r3.anchor: فالآية بمعزل عنه إذ لا يتحقق في ذلك الترك معنى الإنصات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p240/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p240/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p240/r4.claim: The affirmative verbs قرئ and استمعوا do not themselves carry a general sense, so the verse contains no explicit formula of generality.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p240/r4.anchor: ليس في الآية صيغة من صيغ العموم لأن الذي فيها فعلان هما ( قرىء ) ( واستمعوا )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p240/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p240/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p240/r5.claim: إذا generalizes circumstances or times, not kinds of recitation; generality of time or circumstance does not itself entail generality across people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p240/r5.anchor: ومعنى الشرط المستفاد من ( إذا ) يقتضي إلا عموم الأحوال أو الأزمان دون القراءات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p312#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p312#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p312#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed after the Prophet recited in an obligatory prayer and his Companions recited loudly behind him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p312#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ أصحابه وراءه رافعين أصواتهم فنزلت هذه الآية قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p312#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p312#2/r2.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p312#2/r2.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib says the verse addressed polytheists who urged one another to drown out the Qurʾān when the Prophet prayed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p312#2/r2.anchor: لا تسمعوا لهذا القرآن والغوا فيه فنزلت هذه الآية قاله سعيد بن المسيب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p312#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p312#2/r3.speaker: الزهري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p312#2/r3.claim: Al-Zuhrī says it concerned an Anṣārī youth who recited whenever the Prophet recited.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p312#2/r3.anchor: قرأ هو فنزلت هذه الآية قاله الزهري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p312#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p312#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p312#2/r4.claim: Qatāda says the verse addressed people who spoke during prayer in its earliest period, even asking one another how many units they had prayed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p312#2/r4.anchor: كذا وكذا فنزلت هذه الآية قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p312#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p312#2/r5.speaker: عائشة وسعيد بن جبير وعطاء ومجاهد وعمرو بن دينار
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p312#2/r5.claim: A fifth reported occasion makes the verse a command to listen silently to the Friday preacher; it is related from ʿĀʾisha, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿAṭāʾ, Mujāhid, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, and others.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p312#2/r5.anchor: نزلت تأمر بالإنصات للامام في الخطبة يوم الجمعة روي عن عائشة وسعيد بن جبير وعطاء ومجاهد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r1.claim: Because the Quran is insight, guidance, and mercy, God commands respectful silence while it is recited, unlike the Quraysh disbelievers’ call to drown it out in 41:26.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r1.anchor: لما ذكر تعالى أن القرآن بصائر للناس وهدى ورحمة، أمر تعالى بالإنصات عند تلاوته إعظاما له واحتراما،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r2.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r2.claim: Abu Musa reports the Prophet’s instruction that the imam is followed: congregants say the takbir after him and listen quietly when he recites; Ibn Kathir says this especially applies in obligatory prayers with audible recitation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r2.anchor: من حديث أبي موسى الأشعري، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r3.claim: The Sunan also transmit the imam-listening report from Abu Hurayra; Muslim authenticated it but did not include it in his collection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r3.anchor: وكذلك رواه أهل السنن من حديث أبي هريرة (4) وصححه مسلم بن الحجاج أيضا، ولم يخرجه في كتابه (5)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that people used to speak during prayer and were ordered to be silent when this verse and another verse were revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r4.anchor: وقال إبراهيم بن مسلم الهجري، عن أبي عياض، عن أبي هريرة قال: كانوا يتكلمون في الصلاة، فلما نزلت هذه الآية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r5.claim: Ibn Masud says worshippers used to exchange greetings during prayer; this verse came to prohibit the practice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r5.anchor: قال ابن مسعود: كنا يسلم بعضنا على بعض في الصلاة: سلام على فلان، وسلام على فلان، فجاء القرآن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r6.claim: Ibn Masud rebuked people reciting along with the imam, citing this verse as God’s command to listen and be quiet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r6.anchor: حدثنا المحاربي، عن داود بن أبي هند، عن بشير بن جابر قال: صلى ابن مسعود، فسمع ناسا يقرءون مع الإمام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r7.speaker: الزهري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r7.claim: Al-Zuhri says the verse was revealed about an Ansari youth who repeated whatever the Prophet recited.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r7.anchor: وحدثني أبو السائب، حدثنا حفص، عن أشعث، عن الزهري قال: نزلت هذه الآية في فتى من الأنصار،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r8.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that after a loud prayer the Prophet asked whether anyone had recited with him, then said he felt contested in the Quran; people stopped reciting along. The report is in Ahmad and the Sunan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p536/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انصرف من صلاة جهر فيها بالقراءة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r1.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r1.claim: Al-Tirmidhi grades the report about reciting along with the imam hasan; Abu Hatim al-Razi authenticates it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r1.anchor: وقال الترمذي: "هذا حديث حسن". وصححه أبو حاتم الرازي.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r2.speaker: الزهري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r2.claim: Al-Zuhri says followers should not recite aloud behind the imam; the imam’s recitation suffices, while they recite silently in quiet prayers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r2.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن المبارك، عن يونس عن الزهري قال: لا يقرأ من وراء الإمام فيما يجهر به الإمام، تكفيهم قراءة الإمام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r3.speaker: الشافعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r3.claim: One scholarly view, the early position of al-Shafiʿi, Malik’s position, and a report from Ahmad, holds that followers need not recite in the imam’s audible portions, relying on the cited evidence.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r3.anchor: وهو أحد قولي الشافعي، وهو القديم كمذهب مالك، ورواية عن أحمد بن حنبل، لما ذكرناه من الأدلة المتقدمة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r4.claim: Al-Shafiʿi’s later position is that the follower recites only al-Fatiha during the imam’s pauses; a group of Companions, Successors, and later scholars held this view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r4.anchor: وقال في الجديد: يقرأ الفاتحة فقط في سكتات الإمام، وهو قول طائفة من الصحابة والتابعين فمن بعدهم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأحمد بن حنبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r5.claim: Abu Hanifa and Ahmad say a follower need not recite in either quiet or audible prayer, citing the report that an imam’s recitation counts for the follower.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r5.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة وأحمد بن حنبل: لا يجب على المأموم قراءة أصلا في السرية ولا الجهرية، لما ورد في الحديث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r6.speaker: جابر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r6.claim: The report that whoever has an imam has the imam’s recitation is transmitted from Jabir as Prophetic by Ahmad, but as a Companion statement in Malik’s Muwatta; the latter is more authentic.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r6.anchor: رواه الإمام أحمد في مسنده عن جابر مرفوعا، وهو في موطأ مالك عن وهب بن كيسان، عن جابر موقوفا، وهذا أصح.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r7.speaker: البخاري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r7.claim: Al-Bukhari wrote a separate treatise on the issue and chose that followers must recite in both quiet and audible prayers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r7.anchor: وقد أفرد لها الإمام أبو عبد الله البخاري مصنفا على حدة (3) واختار وجوب القراءة خلف الإمام في السرية والجهرية أيضا،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ali ibn Abi Talha, interprets the command as applying to obligatory prayer; the same is reported from Abdullah ibn al-Mughaffal.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r8.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس قوله: {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} يعني: في الصلاة المفروضة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r9.speaker: عبيد بن عمير وعطاء بن أبي رباح
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r9.claim: When asked to listen to a preacher, Ubayd ibn Umayr and Ata ibn Abi Rabah said this verse applies only in prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537/r9.anchor: رأيت عبيد بن عمير وعطاء بن أبي رباح يتحدثان، والقاص يقص،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says the verse concerns prayer; several transmitters report the same interpretation from him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r1.anchor: وقال سفيان الثوري، عن أبي هاشم إسماعيل بن كثير، عن مجاهد في قوله: {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} قال: في الصلاة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says there is no objection to speaking when someone recites outside prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r2.anchor: وقال عبد الرزاق، عن الثوري، عن ليث، عن مجاهد قال: لا بأس إذا قرأ الرجل في غير الصلاة أن يتكلم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, Qatada, al-Shaʿbi, al-Suddi, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd also interpret the command as applying to prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r3.anchor: وكذا قال سعيد بن جبير، والضحاك، وإبراهيم النخعي، وقتادة، والشعبي، والسدي، وعبد الرحمن ابن زيد بن أسلم: أن المراد بذلك في الصلاة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r4.claim: Mujahid and Ata also apply the command to prayer and the Friday sermon.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r4.anchor: وقال شعبة، عن منصور، سمعت إبراهيم بن أبي حرة يحدث أنه سمع مجاهدا يقول في هذه الآية: {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} قال: في الصلاة والخطبة يوم الجمعة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says the command applies in prayer and during remembrance gatherings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r5.anchor: عن الحسن قال: في الصلاة وعند الذكر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r6.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says silence is due on Eid al-Adha, Eid al-Fitr, Friday, and during the imam’s audible recitation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r6.anchor: سمعت سعيد بن جبير يقول في قوله: {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} قال: الإنصات يوم الأضحى، ويوم الفطر، ويوم الجمعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r7.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r7.claim: Ibn Jarir chooses that the command covers listening in prayer and during the sermon, based on reports requiring silence behind the imam and during a sermon.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r7.anchor: وهذا اختيار ابن جرير أن المراد بذلك [الإنصات في الصلاة وفي الخطبة؛ لما جاء في الأحاديث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r8.claim: Mujahid disliked followers saying anything when the imam recites a verse of fear or mercy; they should remain silent.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه كره إذا مر الإمام بآية خوف أو بآية رحمة أن يقول أحد من خلفه شيئا، قال: السكوت.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r9.claim: Al-Hasan says that when one sits with the Quran, one should listen quietly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r9.anchor: عن الحسن: إذا جلست إلى القرآن، فأنصت له.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r10.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that listening to a Quran verse earns a multiplied good deed and reciting it becomes light on Judgment Day; Ahmad alone transmits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p537#2/r10.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

JISHUMI:v4p2832/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r1.claim: Quran derives from gathering: stars gather, menstrual blood gathers in the womb, and blood gathers in the body during purity; recitation is reading and its root sense is following.
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r1.anchor: القرآن: أصله الجمع، ومنه قرأت النجوم: اجتمعت

JISHUMI:v4p2832/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r2.anchor: والإنصات: الإمساك عن الكلام، أنصت ينصت إنصاتا

JISHUMI:v4p2832/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r3.speaker: author
