JISHUMI:v4p2832/r3.claim: القرآن is nominative as the subject substitute of a passive verb, since the verb is predicated of it.
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r3.anchor: رفع القرآن لأنه اسم ما لم يسم فاعله

JISHUMI:v4p2832/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r4.claim: لعل expresses hope or expectation and can also mean the purpose particle كي.

JISHUMI:v4p2832/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود وأبو هريرة والزهري ومجاهد والضحاك والسدي والحسن وقتادة وعبيد بن عمير وعطاء بن أبي رباح
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r5.claim: These authorities say the verse was revealed about prayer, where people spoke and greeted one another and were then ordered to listen.
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r5.anchor: قيل: نزلت الآية في الصلاة، وكانوا يتكلمون فيها

JISHUMI:v4p2832/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that it was revealed about an Anṣārī youth who recited along whenever the Prophet recited.
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r6.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة أنه أنزلت في فتى من الأنصار

JISHUMI:v4p2832/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وجماعة
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r7.claim: Another report places the revelation in the context of the Friday sermon.
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r7.anchor: وقيل: نزلت الآية في الخطبة، عن سعيد بن جبير وجماعة

JISHUMI:v4p2832/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة والكلبي
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r8.claim: Another report connects it to raised voices behind the Prophet during prayer when Paradise and Hell were mentioned.
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r8.anchor: ذكر الجنة والنار، عن أبي هريرة والكلبي

JISHUMI:v4p2832/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r9.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r9.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib says it answered polytheists who told one another to ignore the Quran and make noise when it was recited.
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r9.anchor: نزلت الآية جوابا لهم، عن سعيد بن المسيب

JISHUMI:v4p2832/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r10.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r10.claim: When asked, Ahmad ibn Hanbal said the community agreed that the verse was revealed about prayer.
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r10.anchor: وسئل أحمد بن حنبل عن ذلك، فقال

JISHUMI:v4p2832/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r11.speaker: شيخنا أبو حامد
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r11.claim: Abu Hamid links the command to the preceding description of Quran as insight, guidance, and mercy: listening and reflection lead to truth.
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r11.anchor: لما تقدم أن القرآن بصائر وهدى ورحمة

JISHUMI:v4p2832/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r12.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r12.claim: Abu Muslim says this completes the Prophet's answer to polytheists asking about the Hour and signs: the Quran is inimitable, so they should listen and reflect.
JISHUMI:v4p2832/r12.anchor: إن القرآن معجز، فإذا قرئ فاستمعوا فتدبروا لتعلموا، عن أبي مسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#2/r1.claim: On its apparent meaning, the verse requires listening and silence whenever the Qur’an is recited, both in prayer and outside it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#2/r1.anchor: ظاهره وجوب الاستماع والإنصات وقت قراءة القرآن في صلاة وغير صلاة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#2/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#2/r2.claim: One account says people talked during prayer, prompting the verse; silence when a group hears Qur’an then became a practice outside prayer too.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : كانوا يتكلمون في الصلاة فنزلت ، ثم صار سنة في غير الصلاة أن ينصت القوم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#2/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#2/r3.claim: Another explanation is that the command concerns listening when the Messenger recites Qur’an as it is revealed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#2/r3.anchor: وقيل معناه : وإذا تلا عليكم الرسول القرآن عند نزوله فاستمعوا له

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#2/r4.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#2/r4.claim: A further explanation takes ‘listen to it’ to mean act on the Qur’an’s contents and do not go beyond them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p181#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : معنى فاستمعوا له : فاعملوا بما فيه ولا تجاوزوه

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290/r1.claim: Listening means attending to the Qurʾan's recitation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290/r1.anchor: أي لقراءته . { وأنصتوا } أي لا تقابلوه بكلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290/r2.claim: Silence means neither answering the recitation with speech nor turning away from it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290/r2.anchor: { وأنصتوا } أي لا تقابلوه بكلام ولا إعراض

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290/r3.claim: Mujahid says the instruction was revealed for a congregant behind the imam, who should listen rather than recite.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290/r3.anchor: أحدها : أنها نزلت في المأموم خلف الإمام ينصت ولا يقرأ , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290/r4.speaker: عائشة وعطاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290/r4.claim: ʿAʾisha and ʿAtaʾ say it concerns listening quietly to the Friday sermon without speaking.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290/r4.anchor: والثاني : أنها نزلت في خطبة الجمعة ينصت الحاضر لاستماعها ولا يتكلم , قالته عائشة , وعطاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that people used to greet one another during prayer; the Qurʾanic command came to stop that practice.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290/r5.anchor: ما قاله ابن مسعود : كنا يسلم بعضنا على بعض في الصلاة , سلام على فلان , سلام على فلان , فجاء القرآن

MUJAHID:v1p254#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p254#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p254#3/r1.claim: Mujahid reports that this verse was revealed while the Prophet prayed and heard a young Ansari reciting; the account adds that afterward he saw no harm in recitation or remembrance.
MUJAHID:v1p254#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الصلاة فسمع قراءة فتى من الأنصار فنزل

NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#3/r1.claim: The apparent command requires listening and silence whenever the Qur'an is recited, both in prayer and outside it.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#3/r1.anchor: ظاهره وجوب الاستماع والإنصات وقت قراءة القرآن فى الصلاة وغيرها

NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#3/r2.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#3/r2.claim: Another interpretation is that the command concerns listening when the Messenger recited the Qur'an to people as it was revealed.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#3/r2.anchor: وقيل معناه إذا تلاعليكم الرسول القرآن عند نزوله فاستمعوا له

NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#3/r3.speaker: جمهور الصحابة
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#3/r3.claim: Most Companions apply the verse to the follower listening in congregational prayer.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#3/r3.anchor: وجمهور الصحابة رضى الله عنهم على أنه فى استماع المؤتم وقيل فى استماع الخطبة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#3/r4.claim: Other views limit it to the sermon or cover both the sermon and prayer; the author prefers the combined application.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#3/r4.anchor: وقيل فى استماع الخطبة وقيل فيهما وهو الأصح

QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو هريرة وجابر والزهري وعبيد الله بن عمير وعطاء بن أبي رباح وسعيد بن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r1.claim: These authorities say the command was revealed about listening in prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r1.anchor: روي عن ابن مسعود وأبي هريرة وجابر والزهري وعبيد الله بن عمير وعطاء بن أبي رباح وسعيد بن المسيب

QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r2.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r2.claim: Saʿid says polytheists urged one another to drown out the Prophet's recitation during prayer; the challenge appears in 41:26.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r2.anchor: قال سعيد: كان المشركون يأتون رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا صلى فيقول بعضهم لبعض بمكة:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وعطاء وعمرو بن دينار وزيد بن أسلم والقاسم بن مخيمرة ومسلم بن يسار وشهر بن حوشب وعبد الله بن المبارك
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r3.claim: These authorities say the verse was revealed about listening during the Friday sermon.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r3.anchor: وقيل: إنها نزلت في الخطبة قاله سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وعطاء وعمرو بن دينار

QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r4.speaker: ابن العربي والنقاش
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r4.claim: Ibn al-Arabi calls the sermon occasion weak because Quran is brief and silence applies throughout; al-Naqqash notes the verse is Meccan, before sermons or Friday prayer in Mecca.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r4.anchor: وهذا ضعيف لأن القرآن فيها قليل، والإنصات يجب في جميعها قاله ابن العربي. النقاش: والآية مكية

QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r5.claim: A report cited by al-Tabari applies the command to both Eids, Friday, and all Quran recited aloud by an imam; Qurtubi says this gathers the verse and Sunna.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r5.anchor: وذكر الطبري عن سعيد بن جبير أيضا أن هذا في الإنصات يوم الأضحى ويوم الفطر ويوم الجمعة

QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r6.speaker: النقاش
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r6.claim: Al-Naqqash says interpreters agree that listening applies in obligatory and voluntary prayers.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r6.anchor: قال النقاش: أجمع أهل التفسير أن هذا الاستماع في الصلاة المكتوبة وغير المكتوبة.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r7.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r7.claim: Al-Nahhas says the wording applies generally unless evidence restricts it.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r7.anchor: النحاس: وفي اللغة يجب أن يكون في كل شيء، إلا أن يدل دليل على اختصاص شيء.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r8.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj allows the command to mean work according to the Quran and do not transgress it.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r8.anchor: وقال الزجاج: يجوز أن يكون «فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا» اعملوا بما فيه ولا تجاوزوه.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r9.claim: Inṣāt is silence for listening, attending, and focusing; Arabic has both أنصت and نصت, illustrated in poetry.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r9.anchor: والإنصات السكوت للاستماع والإصغاء والمراعاة. أنصت ينصت إنصاتا ونصت أيضا قال الشاعر:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r10.speaker: بعضهم
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r10.claim: Some restrict the command to the Prophet so Companions could learn from him; Qurtubi rejects this as unlikely and prefers the general wording and mercy clause.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r10.anchor: وقال بعضهم في قوله «فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا»: كان هذا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خاصا ليعيه عنه أصحابه.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r11.speaker: عبد الجبار بن أحمد
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r11.claim: Abd al-Jabbar contrasts Muslim listening with polytheist disruption in 41:26 and notes the jinn's listening in 46:29.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204/r11.anchor: إن المشركين كانوا يكثرون اللغط والشغب تعنتا وعنادا على ما حكاه الله عنهم

QURTUBI-FULL:7:204#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204#2/r1.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204#2/r1.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says companions answered the Prophet's basmala and recited with him aloud, prompting the command to stop responding.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204#2/r1.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قرأ في الصلاة أجابه من وراءه

QURTUBI-FULL:7:204#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204#2/r2.claim: Qatada says people asked worshippers how many cycles were done and remained, prompting the command.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204#2/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة في هذه الآية: كان الرجل يأتي وهم في الصلاة فيسألهم كم صليتم، كم بقي

QURTUBI-FULL:7:204#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says people discussed their needs during prayer, prompting the verse's promise of mercy.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204#2/r3.anchor: وعن مجاهد أيضا: كانوا يتكلمون في الصلاة بحاجتهم فنزل قوله تعالى: { لعلكم ترحمون }

QURTUBI-FULL:7:204#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204#2/r4.claim: Qurtubi refers to the dispute on reciting behind an imam in al-Fatiha and the later discussion of Friday sermons in al-Jumuʿa.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:204#2/r4.anchor: وقد مضى في الفاتحة الاختلاف في قراءة المأموم خلف الإمام. ويأتي في «الجمعة» حكم الخطبة

QASHANI:7:201-205/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:201-205/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:201-205/r5.claim: Listening to the Quran means listening to God and listening only from Him.
QASHANI:7:201-205/r5.anchor: إلى الله ولا تستمعوا إلا منه

QASHANI:7:201-205/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:201-205/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:201-205/r6.claim: Be silent from self-talk and everything besides God, since God is the one speaking in the recitation.

QASHANI:7:201-205/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:201-205/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:201-205/r7.claim: They may receive mercy through the manifestation of the speaker in His speech with His attributes and acts.
QASHANI:7:201-205/r7.anchor: برحمة تجلي المتكلم في كلامه بصفاته وأفعاله

RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r1.claim: After declaring the Qur'an clear proofs, guidance, and mercy, God follows by commanding listeners to hear it and be silent.
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r1.anchor: لما عظم شأن القرآن بقوله : { هاذا بصائر من ربكم } ( الأعراف : 203 ) أردفه بقوله : { وإذا قرىء القرءان

RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r2.claim: Inṣāt means silence; naṣata, anṣata, and intaṣata are used with the same meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r2.anchor: الإنصات السكوت والاستماع ، يقال : نصت ، وأنصت ، وانتصت ، بمعنى واحد

RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r3.claim: The verse is phrased as a command, whose apparent force is obligation, so listening and silence appear obligatory; scholars differ over its scope.
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r3.anchor: لا شك أن قوله : { فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا } أمره ، وظاهر الأمر للوجوب

RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r4.speaker: الحسن وأهل الظاهر
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan and the literalists apply the command generally: whenever anyone recites Qur'an, everyone must listen silently, including passersby and children's teachers.
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r4.anchor: القول الأول : وهو قول الحسن وقول أهل الظاهر أنا نجري هذه الآية على عمومها

RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r5.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that people used to talk during prayer, so this verse was revealed commanding silence.
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه : كانوا يتكلمون في الصلاة فنزلت هذه الآية ، وأمروا بالإنصات

RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r6.claim: Qatāda says people in prayer talked about their needs and answered arrivals asking how much they had prayed or how much remained; the verse was revealed about this.
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة : كان الرجل يأتي وهم في الصلاة فيسألهم ، كم صليتم وكم بقي ؟

RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet and companions recited aloud in obligatory prayer, confusing one another, and the verse then came down.
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الصلاة المكتوبة وقرأ أصحابه وراءه رافعين أصواتهم

RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r8.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and his companions take the verse to prohibit followers from reciting aloud behind the imam.
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r8.anchor: فخلطوا عليه ، فنزلت هذه الآية وهو قول أبي حنيفة وأصحابه

RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وعطاء والشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r9.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid, and ʿAṭāʾ, with this view also transmitted from al-Shāfiʿī, understand the verse as requiring silence during the sermon.
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r9.anchor: وهذا قول سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وعطاء وهذا القول منقول عن الشافعي رحمه الله

RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r10.claim: Rāzī finds restricting the verse to the sermon highly unlikely: idhā connects an event to its consequence but does not imply repetition, as in a one-time conditional divorce.
RAZI-FULL:v15p83#2/r10.anchor: وأقول هذا القول في غاية البعد لأن لفظة إذا تفيد الارتباط ، ولا تفيد التكرار

RAZI-FULL:v15p84/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p84/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p84/r1.claim: Since idhā does not entail repetition, one occasion of Qur'an recitation fulfills the command; the sermon reading suffices, leaving no further indication in the wording.
RAZI-FULL:v15p84/r1.anchor: قوله : { وإذا قرىء القرءان فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا } لا يفيد إلا وجوب الإنصات مرة واحدة

RAZI-FULL:v15p84/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p84/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p84/r2.claim: On al-Shāfiʿī's position the imam pauses so the follower may recite al-Fātiḥa; Abū Salama says the imam has two pauses in which one may seize an opportunity to recite.
RAZI-FULL:v15p84/r2.anchor: عند الشافعي رحمه الله : يسكت الإمام ، وحينئذ يقرأ المأموم الفاتحة

RAZI-FULL:v15p84/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p84/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p84/r3.claim: Rāzī rejects the pause defense: if the imam's pause is obligatory it lacks consensus, and if optional the imam may recite while the follower does, violating listening; the duration may be too short and makes the imam subordinate.
RAZI-FULL:v15p84/r3.anchor: ولقائل أن يقول : سكوت الإمام إما أن نقول : إنه من الواجبات أو ليس من الواجبات والأول باطل بالإجماع

RAZI-FULL:v15p84/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p84/r4.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v15p84/r4.claim: Al-Wāḥidī proposes that inṣāt means refraining from speaking aloud, so Arabs can call a silent reader who cannot be heard anṣat.
RAZI-FULL:v15p84/r4.anchor: وذكر الواحدي سؤالا ثانيا على التمسك بالآية . فقال : إن الإنصات هو ترك الجهر والعرب تسمي تارك الجهر منصتا

RAZI-FULL:v15p84/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p84/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p84/r5.claim: Rāzī replies that reciting, even silently, prevents listening: listening means full attention, as in God's command to Moses, so the command to listen entails a ban on recitation.
RAZI-FULL:v15p84/r5.anchor: فالاستماع عبارة عن كونه بحيث يحيط بذلك الكلام المسموع على الوجه الكامل ، قال تعالى لموسى عليه السلام : { وأنا اخترتك فاستمع لما يوحى }

RAZI-FULL:v15p84#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p84#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p84#2/r1.claim: Rāzī calls it sound that jurists allow Qur'an's general wording to be specified by a solitary report: the specific hadith requiring al-Fātiḥa in prayer limits this verse's general command.
RAZI-FULL:v15p84#2/r1.anchor: الفقهاء أجمعوا على أنه يجوز تخصيص عموم القرآن / بخبر الواحد

RAZI-FULL:v15p84#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p84#2/r2.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v15p84#2/r2.claim: The Prophet's reports say there is no prayer for one who has not recited the Opening and no prayer except with the Opening; Rāzī treats them as more specific than the verse.
RAZI-FULL:v15p84#2/r2.anchor: إلا أن قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( لا صلاة لمن لم يقرأ بفاتحة الكتاب ) وقوله : ( لا صلاة إلا بفاتحة الكتاب )

RAZI-FULL:v15p84#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p84#2/r3.speaker: مالك والشافعي في قوله القديم
RAZI-FULL:v15p84#2/r3.claim: Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī in his earlier position bar followers from reciting al-Fātiḥa in audible prayers, based on this text, but require it in silent prayers, which the verse does not address.
RAZI-FULL:v15p84#2/r3.anchor: مذهب مالك وهو القول القديم للشافعي أنه لا يجوز للمأموم أن يقرأ الفاتحة في الصلوات الجهرية

RAZI-FULL:v15p84#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p84#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p84#2/r4.claim: Rāzī's fifth view addresses disbelievers at the start of revelation; applying the verse to followers behind an imam would sever its link to the preceding discussion of demands for signs and the Qur'an's sufficiency.
RAZI-FULL:v15p84#2/r4.anchor: وفي الآية قول خامس وهو أن قوله تعالى : { وإذا قرىء القرءان فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا } خطاب مع الكفار في ابتداء التبليغ

RAZI-FULL:v15p84#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p84#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p84#2/r5.claim: The disbelievers must listen as the Prophet recites, so they can grasp the Qur'an's eloquence and knowledge, recognize its miraculous proof of his truth, and see why other miracles are unnecessary.
RAZI-FULL:v15p84#2/r5.anchor: استمعوا له وأنصتوا حتى يقفوا على فصاحته ، ويحيطوا بما فيه من العلوم الكثيرة

RAZI-FULL:v15p85/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p85/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p85/r1.claim: Because disbelievers had said to drown out the Qur'an rather than listen, Rāzī sees the command to listen silently as a fitting response that lets them encounter its inimitability.
RAZI-FULL:v15p85/r1.anchor: حكى عن الكفار أنهم قالوا : { لا تسمعوا لهاذا القرءان والغوا فيه لعلكم تغلبون } ( فصلت : 26 )

RAZI-FULL:v15p85/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p85/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p85/r2.claim: The preceding verse definitively calls the Qur'an mercy for believers, so conditional hope of mercy fits disbelievers instead: listening may reveal its signs, lead them to believe, and make them recipients of mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v15p85/r2.anchor: فحكم تعالى بكون هذا القرآن رحمة للمؤمنين على سبيل القطع والجزم

RAZI-FULL:v15p85/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p85/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p85/r3.claim: Rāzī concludes that the audience is disbelievers hearing the Prophet at the start of revelation and the call; this preserves the order and defeats use of the verse for congregational recitation.
RAZI-FULL:v15p85/r3.anchor: هذا الخطاب ما يتناول المؤمنين ، وإنما تناول الكفار في أول زمان تبليغ الوحي والدعوة

RAZI-FULL:v22p41#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p41#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p41#2/r14.claim: Inṣāt requires both listening and silence; when either is absent, it is not called inṣāt, as the verse joins listening and attentive silence.
RAZI-FULL:v22p41#2/r14.anchor: والانصات سكوت مع استماع ومتى انفك أحدهما عن الآخر لا يقال له إنصات

STUDYQURAN:7:204/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r1.claim: The near-synonymous commands to hearken and listen emphasize careful attention to the Quran's sacred recitation.
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r1.anchor: employing two words that are nearly synonyms, serves to emphasize the care with which one should listen

STUDYQURAN:7:204/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r2.claim: Careful listening entails understanding the Quran's meaning, reflecting on its teachings, and acting on its prescriptions.
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r2.anchor: paying full attention in order to understand its meaning as well as reflecting upon its teachings (Aj, Ṭ) and acting according to its prescriptions

STUDYQURAN:7:204/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r3.anchor: Listen translates anṣitū, which connotes listening silently

STUDYQURAN:7:204/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r4.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r4.claim: Some say silence was particularly important when the Prophet recited the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r4.anchor: some indicate was particularly important when the Prophet was reciting the Quran (Q)

STUDYQURAN:7:204/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r5.claim: In communal prayer, those behind the imam must silently attend to his Quranic recitation, neither talking nor reciting aloud themselves.
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r5.anchor: requiring all those praying behind the imam to be silent and listen attentively to the Quranic passages

STUDYQURAN:7:204/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r6.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r6.claim: Some commentators apply attentive listening whenever one hears the Quran recited, in any context.
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r6.anchor: Some commentators assert that the command to listen attentively to the recited Quran applies to any context in which one hears it

STUDYQURAN:7:204/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r7.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r7.claim: Silent, receptive listening is seen as cultivating pure servitude to God or entry into His Presence as the ultimate Speaker behind the recitation.
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r7.anchor: Listening silently and with pure receptivity to the recited Quran is considered by some as a means of developing the quality of pure servitude

STUDYQURAN:7:204/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r8.claim: Because the preceding verse calls the Quran a mercy, attentive hearing of its recitation is a means of receiving mercy.
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r8.anchor: Since the Quran is described in v. 203 as a mercy, one should hearken to its recited words so one may receive mercy

STUDYQURAN:7:204/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r9.speaker: Ibn ʿAjībah
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAjībah says mercy is the closest thing to the person listening to the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:7:204/r9.anchor: Ibn ʿAjībah states that “mercy is the closest thing to the one listening to the Quran.”

TAB-FULL:v10p658/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r1.claim: Believers should attend carefully to recited Qurʾān to understand its verses and heed admonitions; they should be silent to comprehend and reflect rather than engage in distracting talk.

TAB-FULL:v10p658/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r2.claim: Listening brings God's mercy through heeding admonitions, learning from examples, and applying the duties God laid down in the Qurʾān.
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r2.anchor: ليرحمكم ربكم باتعاظكم بمواعظه، واعتباركم بعبره

TAB-FULL:v10p658/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r3.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r3.claim: Some exegetes restrict the listening command to prayer behind an imam: one who hears the imam recite must listen; they say the verse was revealed for this situation.
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r3.anchor: فقال بعضهم: ذلك حال كون المصلي في الصلاة خلف إمام يأتم به، وهو يسمع قراءة الإمام عليه أن يسمع لقراءته

TAB-FULL:v10p658/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r4.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r4.claim: ʿAbd Allāh recalls that worshippers used to greet one another during prayer, after which the Qurʾānic command came.
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r4.anchor: عن المسيب بن رافع، قال: كان عبد الله يقول: " كنا يسلم بعضنا على بعض في الصلاة

TAB-FULL:v10p658/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r5.claim: Abū Hurayra says people spoke during prayer, then this verse and another were revealed and they were ordered to be silent.
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r5.anchor: عن أبي عياض، عن أبي هريرة، قال: " كانوا يتكلمون في الصلاة، فلما نزلت هذه الآية: {وإذا قرئ القرآن} [الأعراف: 204] والآية الأخرى، أمروا بالإنصات

TAB-FULL:v10p658/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r6.speaker: الزهري
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r6.claim: Al-Zuhrī says the verse was revealed about an Anṣārī youth who repeated each passage whenever the Prophet recited it.
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r6.anchor: عن أشعث، عن الزهري، قال: " نزلت هذه الآية في فتى من الأنصار كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كلما قرأ شيئا قرأه

TAB-FULL:v10p658/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿūd rebuked people reciting along with the imam and reminded them that God commanded them to listen and be silent.
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r7.anchor: عن داود بن أبي هند، عن بشير بن جابر، قال: صلى ابن مسعود، فسمع ناسا، يقرءون مع الإمام

TAB-FULL:v10p658/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r8.speaker: عبيد بن عمير وعطاء بن أبي رباح
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r8.claim: ʿUbayd b. ʿUmayr and ʿAṭāʾ b. Abī Rabāḥ say the listening command applies specifically in prayer; they continued talking while a storyteller spoke.
TAB-FULL:v10p658/r8.anchor: رأيت عبيد بن عمير وعطاء بن أبي رباح يتحدثان والقاص يقص، فقلت: ألا تستمعان إلى الذكر

SULAMI:v1p252#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p252#3/r1.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p252#3/r1.claim: Listen outwardly so the heart can hear and understand God's address; learn from its admonitions, since good comportment and the blessings of hearing lead to mercy and the etiquette of servanthood granted to the elect.
SULAMI:v1p252#3/r1.anchor: قيل : فيه استمعوا له بآذانكم لعلكم تسمعون بقلوبكم وتفهمون مراد مخاطبة الحق إياكم ، وتأدبوا بلطائف مواعظه

SULAMI:v1p252#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p252#3/r2.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p252#3/r2.claim: Silence is part of proper listening: attend to the blessings that arise through audition without seeking a personal benefit.
SULAMI:v1p252#3/r2.anchor: وقيل في قوله : ﴿ وأنصتوا ﴾ أي من آداب الاستماع الإنصات والاشتغال ، بما يبدو

TAB-FULL:v10p661/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p661/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p661/r1.claim: The believers should incline their hearing to the Quran so they understand its signs and take lessons from its admonitions.
TAB-FULL:v10p661/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن هذه الآية: " {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} [الأعراف: 204] قال: نزلت في رفع الأصوات

TAB-FULL:v10p661/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p661/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v10p661/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra says the verse was revealed when people behind the Messenger raised their voices during prayer.
TAB-FULL:v10p661/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن هذه الآية: " {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} [الأعراف: 204] قال: نزلت في رفع الأصوات

TAB-FULL:v10p661/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p661/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p661/r3.claim: Mujahid says the command concerns prayer.
TAB-FULL:v10p661/r3.anchor: عن أبي هاشم إسماعيل بن كثير، عن مجاهد، في قوله: " {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} [الأعراف: 204] قال: في الصلاة

TAB-FULL:v10p661/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p661/r4.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
TAB-FULL:v10p661/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib says the command concerns prayer.
TAB-FULL:v10p661/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، عن سعيد بن المسيب: " {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} [الأعراف: 204] قال: في الصلاة

TAB-FULL:v10p661/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p661/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p661/r5.anchor: عن ليث، عن مجاهد: " {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} [الأعراف: 204] قال: في الصلاة المكتوبة

TAB-FULL:v10p661/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p661/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v10p661/r6.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the command concerns the obligatory prayer.
TAB-FULL:v10p661/r6.anchor: عن الحكم، عن سعيد بن جبير: " {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} [الأعراف: 204] قال: في الصلاة المكتوبة

TAB-FULL:v10p661/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p661/r7.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v10p661/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak says the command concerns the obligatory prayer.
TAB-FULL:v10p661/r7.anchor: عن جويبر، عن الضحاك، قال: «في الصلاة المكتوبة»

TAB-FULL:v10p662/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r1.claim: Ibrahim says the command concerns the obligatory prayer.
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r1.anchor: عن مغيرة، عن إبراهيم، قال: «في الصلاة المكتوبة»

TAB-FULL:v10p662/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r2.claim: Qatada says people initially talked about their needs during prayer, and this command was revealed to stop that practice.
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} [الأعراف: 204] قال: كانوا يتكلمون في صلاتهم بحوائجهم أول ما فرضت عليهم

TAB-FULL:v10p662/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r3.claim: Qatada describes a person arriving during prayer to ask how many units had been prayed and how many remained before the verse was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r3.anchor: عن قتادة: " {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} [الأعراف: 204] قال: كان الرجل يأتي وهم في الصلاة فيسألهم: كم صليتم؟ كم بقي؟ فأنزل الله

TAB-FULL:v10p662/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r4.speaker: غيره
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r4.claim: An unnamed authority says people raised their voices during prayer when they heard mention of Paradise and Hell, prompting the revelation.
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r4.anchor: وقال غيره: كانوا يرفعون أصواتهم في الصلاة حين يسمعون ذكر الجنة والنار

TAB-FULL:v10p662/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r5.speaker: الزهري
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r5.claim: Al-Zuhri says the Prophet was reciting while another man recited, and the verse was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r5.anchor: عن الزهري، قال: " كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ ورجل يقرأ، فنزلت

TAB-FULL:v10p662/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra says people used to speak during prayer; after the verse came down, he identified it as applying to prayer.
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: " كانوا يتكلمون في الصلاة، فلما نزلت: {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} [الأعراف: 204] قال: هذا في الصلاة

TAB-FULL:v10p662/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r7.speaker: عامر
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r7.claim: Amir says the command concerns the obligatory prayer.
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r7.anchor: عن حريث، عن عامر، قال: «في الصلاة المكتوبة»

TAB-FULL:v10p662/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r8.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says the command applies when the Quran is recited during prayer.
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r8.anchor: عن السدي: " {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} [الأعراف: 204] قال: إذا قرئ في الصلاة

TAB-FULL:v10p662/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse refers to the prescribed prayer.
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له} [الأعراف: 204] يعني: في الصلاة المفروضة

TAB-FULL:v10p662/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r10.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r10.claim: Mujahid says this command concerns prayer.
TAB-FULL:v10p662/r10.anchor: عن أبي هاشم، عن مجاهد قال: " هذا في الصلاة في قوله: {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له}

TAB-FULL:v10p663/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r1.claim: Mujahid distinguishes prayer, where the imam's recitation calls for silence, from recitation outside prayer, when speaking is permitted.
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: «لا بأس إذا قرأ الرجل في غير الصلاة أن يتكلم»

TAB-FULL:v10p663/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r2.claim: Mujahid permits speaking when someone recites the Quran outside prayer.
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: «لا بأس إذا قرأ الرجل في غير الصلاة أن يتكلم»

TAB-FULL:v10p663/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd applies the command to the congregation when the imam stands for prayer.
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا لعلكم ترحمون} [الأعراف: 204] قال: هذا إذا قام الإمام للصلاة

TAB-FULL:v10p663/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r4.speaker: الزهري
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r4.claim: Al-Zuhri says followers should not recite aloud or silently along with an imam's audible recitation; they may recite silently to themselves when he recites inaudibly, and the imam's audible reading suffices even if unheard.
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r4.anchor: عن الزهري، قال: " لا يقرأ من وراء الإمام فيما يجهر به من القراءة، تكفيهم قراءة الإمام وإن لم يسمعهم صوته

TAB-FULL:v10p663/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says remembrance in 7:205 is for obligatory prayer and later stories or recitation are supererogatory; he reports that companions recited behind the Prophet in an obligatory prayer, confusing him, after which 7:204 was revealed for that prayer.
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، أنه كان يقول في هذه: " {واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخيفة} [الأعراف: 205] هذا في المكتوبة

TAB-FULL:v10p663/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r6.claim: Mujahid says the command means listening to the imam during the Friday sermon.
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: " {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} [الأعراف: 204] قال: الإنصات للإمام يوم الجمعة

TAB-FULL:v10p663/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r7.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r7.claim: Another reported view applies the command to listening to the imam when Quran is recited during the sermon.
TAB-FULL:v10p663/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل عني بهذه الآية الأمر بالإنصات للإمام في الخطبة إذا قرئ القرآن في خطبة

TAB-FULL:v10p667/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r1.claim: Mujahid applies the command to both prayer and the Friday sermon.
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r1.anchor: أنه سمع مجاهدا، يقول في هذه الآية: " {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} [الأعراف: 204] قال: في الصلاة، والخطبة يوم الجمعة

TAB-FULL:v10p667/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r2.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r2.claim: Ata says silence is required when a man recites Quran during prayer and when the imam preaches; he also says the same listening obligation applies in Friday prayer and the sermon.
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r2.anchor: عن عطاء، قال: " وجب الصموت في اثنتين: عند الرجل يقرأ القرآن وهو يصلي، وعند الإمام وهو يخطب

TAB-FULL:v10p667/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r3.claim: Mujahid says silence is required in two settings: prayer while the imam recites and Friday while the imam preaches.
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {وإذا قرئ القرآن} [الأعراف: 204] وجب الإنصات، قال: وجب في اثنتين: في الصلاة والإمام يقرأ

TAB-FULL:v10p667/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r4.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r4.claim: Al-Hasan applies silence to the obligatory prayer and to remembrance gatherings.
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r4.anchor: سمع الحسن، يقول: «في الصلاة المكتوبة، وعند الذكر»

TAB-FULL:v10p667/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r5.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says listening is required on the two Eids and Friday, and during the imam's audible recitation in prayer.
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r5.anchor: سمعت سعيد بن جبير، يقول في قوله: " {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا} [الأعراف: 204] قال: الإنصات: يوم الأضحى، ويوم الفطر، ويوم الجمعة

TAB-FULL:v10p667/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r6.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r6.claim: Ata ibn Abi Rabah says the verse requires listening on Friday, and the same applies during prayer.
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r6.anchor: عن عطاء بن أبي رباح، قال: " أوجب الإنصات يوم الجمعة قول الله تعالى: {وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا لعلكم ترحمون} [الأعراف: 204] وفي الصلاة مثل ذلك

TAB-FULL:v10p667/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r7.claim: Tabari says a sound report from the Prophet commands silence when the imam recites.
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r7.anchor: لصحة الخبر عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، أنه قال: «إذا قرأ الإمام فأنصتوا»

TAB-FULL:v10p667/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r8.claim: Tabari prefers requiring attentive listening during an imam's audible prayer recitation for a follower who hears, and during the Friday sermon; Quranic generality, the sound Prophetic report, and consensus on listening to the sermon support this, though authorities differ about following an imam.
TAB-FULL:v10p667/r8.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: أمروا باستماع القرآن في الصلاة إذا قرأ الإمام

TABATABAI:7:201-204/r16.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r16.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r16.claim: Insat means silence while listening; it is also explained as listening in silence.
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r16.anchor: الإنصات السكوت مع استماع، وقيل هو الاستماع مع سكوت

TABATABAI:7:201-204/r17.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r17.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r17.claim: The command is to listen to the Quran and remain silent.

TABRISI:7:204-205/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:204-205/r1.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
TABRISI:7:204-205/r1.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi explains the forms as listening to speech while remaining silent.

TABRISI:7:204-205/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:204-205/r2.speaker: الأزهري
TABRISI:7:204-205/r2.claim: Related forms mean listen to him, fall silent, or be silenced by another person.
TABRISI:7:204-205/r2.anchor: وأنصته وأنصت له وأنصت الرجل سكت وأنصته غيره عن الأزهري

TABRISI:7:204-205/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:204-205/r5.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن مسعود، سعيد بن جبير، سعيد بن المسيب، مجاهد، الزهري، أبو جعفر
TABRISI:7:204-205/r5.claim: They limit the command to prayer behind an imam whose recitation one hears; Muslims had spoken, greeted one another, and answered questions during prayer before being forbidden.
TABRISI:7:204-205/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود وسعيد بن جبير وسعيد بن المسيب ومجاهد والزهري

TABRISI:7:204-205/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:204-205/r6.speaker: عطاء، عمرو بن دينار، زيد بن أسلم
TABRISI:7:204-205/r6.claim: These authorities apply the command to listening to the imam's Friday sermon.
TABRISI:7:204-205/r6.anchor: عن عطاء وعمرو بن دينار وزيد بن أسلم

TABRISI:7:204-205/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:204-205/r7.speaker: الحسن وجماعة
TABRISI:7:204-205/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan and a group say the command applies to both the sermon and prayer.

TABRISI:7:204-205/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:204-205/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:204-205/r8.claim: The strongest view makes listening obligatory only when the imam recites in prayer; outside prayer it is not obligatory by consensus.
TABRISI:7:204-205/r8.anchor: وأقوى الأقوال الأول لأنه لا حال يجب فيها الإنصات لقراءة القرآن إلا حالة قراءة الإمام في الصلاة

TABRISI:7:204-205/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:204-205/r9.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:7:204-205/r9.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh says listening is required during prayer and outside it, clarifying that the latter is recommended.
TABRISI:7:204-205/r9.anchor: وروي عن أبي عبد الله ع أنه قال يجب الإنصات للقرآن في الصلاة وغيرها

TABRISI:7:204-205/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:204-205/r10.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
TABRISI:7:204-205/r10.claim: When Ibn al-Kawwāʾ recited behind ʿAlī, ʿAlī listened silently.

TABRISI:7:204-205/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:204-205/r11.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:7:204-205/r11.claim: Asked whether a hearer must listen, Abū ʿAbd Allāh says yes when Qurʾān is recited in one's presence.
TABRISI:7:204-205/r11.anchor: عن عبد الله بن أبي يعفور عن أبي عبد الله ع قال قلت له الرجل يقرأ القرآن

TABRISI:7:204-205/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:204-205/r12.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:7:204-205/r12.claim: Al-Zajjāj allows the phrase to mean act according to the Qurʾān's contents and do not transgress.
TABRISI:7:204-205/r12.anchor: قال الزجاج: ويجوز أن يكون فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا أي اعملوا بما فيه

TABRISI:7:204-205/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:204-205/r13.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:7:204-205/r13.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says the verse was revealed at the beginning of the Prophet's proclamation so people would learn or understand.
TABRISI:7:204-205/r13.anchor: وقال الجبائي: إنها نزلت في ابتداء التبليغ ليعلموا أو يتفهموا

TABRISI:7:204-205/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:204-205/r14.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
TABRISI:7:204-205/r14.claim: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal says the community agreed that the verse was revealed concerning prayer.
TABRISI:7:204-205/r14.anchor: وقال أحمد بن حنبل: أجمعت الأمة على أنها نزلت في الصلاة

TABRISI:7:204-205/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:204-205/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:204-205/r15.claim: Listening brings mercy through taking admonition from the Qurʾān's exhortations.
TABRISI:7:204-205/r15.anchor: أي لترحموا بذلك وباعتباركم به واتعاظكم بمواعظه

THALABI:v4p322/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p322/r1.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
THALABI:v4p322/r1.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz says الإنصات means listening to every preacher attentively and with consideration.
THALABI:v4p322/r1.anchor: وقال عمر بن عبد العزيز: الإنصات لقول كل واعظ والإنصات الإصغاء والمراعاة

THALABI:v4p322/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p322/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v4p322/r2.claim: Said ibn Jubayr applies the command to silence during the two Eid prayers, Friday, and the imam's audible recitation.
THALABI:v4p322/r2.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: هذا في الإنصات يوم الأضحى ويوم الفطر ويوم الجمعة وفيما يجهر به الإمام

THALABI:v4p322/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p322/r3.speaker: الزجاج
THALABI:v4p322/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj allows the meaning to be act on what is heard and do not go beyond it; hearing God is idiomatically answering a prayer.
THALABI:v4p322/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج: ويجوز أن يكون معنى قوله فاستمعوا وأنصتوا اعملوا بما فيه لا تجاوزوه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r1.claim: Inṣāt means silence for listening; naṣata, anṣata, and intaṣata are equivalent forms.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r1.anchor: الإنصات السكوت للاستماع، يقال: نصت وأنصت وانتصت بمعنى واحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r2.speaker: الأصمعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r2.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says al-Kumayt uses أنصت transitively to mean that all speakers were silenced.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r3.speaker: الكميت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r3.claim: Al-Kumayt's verse uses الإنصات transitively in the sense of silencing someone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r3.anchor: وقد ورد الإنصات متعديا في شعر الكميت (¬5) بمعنى الإسكات وهو قوله (¬6): أبوك الذي أجدى علي بنصره ... فأنصت عني بعده كل قائل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra says the verse came because people used to talk during prayer, after which they were ordered to be silent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r4.anchor: قال أبو هريرة: (كانوا يتكلمون في الصلاة فنزلت هذه الآية وأمروا بالإنصات)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r5.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r5.claim: Qatada says people asked how much prayer remained and discussed their needs while praying, prompting the verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة: (كان الرجل يأتي وهم في الصلاة فيسألهم كم صليتم وكم بقي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r6.speaker: معاوية بن قرة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r6.claim: Muawiya ibn Qurra gives a similar account of the verse's context as prayer-time speech.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r6.anchor: ونحو هذا قال معاوية (¬5) بن قرة (¬6)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r7.claim: Ibn Masud says worshippers used to greet one another by name during prayer, and the verse then came.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r7.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: كنا يسلم بعضنا على بعض في الصلاة؛ سلام على فلان، سلام على فلان، فجاء القرآن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse came when companions recited aloud behind the Prophet in obligatory prayer and disrupted his recitation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (إن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قرأ في الصلاة المكتوبة وقرأ أصحابه وراءه رافعين أصواتهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r9.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra also places the occasion in companions raising their voices behind the Messenger during prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r9.anchor: وروي عن أبي هريرة مثل ذلك (¬1) قال: (نزلت هذه الآية في رفع الأصوات وهم خلف رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r10.claim: A similar account is also transmitted from Ibn Masud.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r10.anchor: وروي أيضا عن ابن مسعود (¬3) مثل هذا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r11.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r11.claim: Al-Kalbi says people raised their voices in prayer when they heard mention of Paradise and Hell, prompting the verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r11.anchor: وقال الكلبي: (كانوا يرفعون أصواتهم في الصلاة حين يسمعون ذكر الجنة والنار فأنزل الله هذه الآية)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r12.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وعطاء وعمرو بن دينار وزيد بن أسلم والقاسم بن مخيمرة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r12.claim: These authorities and others say the verse concerns silence to hear the Friday sermon.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r12.anchor: وهذا قول سعيد (¬5) بن جبير ومجاهد (¬6) وعطاء (¬7) وعمرو (¬8) بن دينار، وزيد بن أسلم (¬9) والقاسم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r13.speaker: ابن المبارك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r13.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak argues for the sermon interpretation: preachers recite this verse before citing Quran during Friday sermons.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p563/r13.anchor: واحتج ابن المبارك (¬2) لهذا القول بأن قال: (لا ترى خطيبا يخطب يوم الجمعة فأراد أن يقرأ في الخطبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r1.speaker: الفراء وأبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r1.claim: Al-Farra and Abu Ishaq prefer the prayer-speech occasion: people talked during obligatory prayer, prompting the prohibition.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r1.anchor: واختار الفراء (¬5)، وأبو إسحاق (¬6) القول الأول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r2.claim: The verse does not prove that a follower may omit al-Fatiha: depending on the account, it bars improper speech, loud recitation, or applies to the sermon.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r2.anchor: ولا حجة في الآية لمن أبى وجوب قراءة الفاتحة في الصلاة خلف الإمام؛ لأن قوله: {وأنصتوا} على القول الأول أمر بالإنصات عن الكلام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r3.speaker: الأوزاعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r3.claim: Al-Awzaʿi says God commanded silence from speech, not Quran recitation, because people had been talking in prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r3.anchor: وقد قال الأوزاعي (¬1): (إن الله أمر بالإنصات عن الكلام لا عن قراءة القرآن لأنهم كانوا يتكلمون في الصلاة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r4.speaker: الشافعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r4.claim: Al-Shafiʿi holds that the verse's requirement is met by the imam's pauses, allowing the follower to recite al-Fatiha then.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r4.anchor: قيل له: حكم الآية ممتثل (¬3) عند الشافعي (¬4) -رضي الله عنه-؛ لأن السنة أن يسكت الإمام ويتنفس فيقرأ المأموم الفاتحة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r5.speaker: أبو سلمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r5.claim: Abu Salama says the imam has two pauses, and the follower may use either for recitation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r5.anchor: كما قال أبو سلمة (¬5): (للإمام سكتتان فاغتنم القراءة في أيهما شئت)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r6.claim: Arabs call a person who does not recite aloud anṣata, even if he reads silently as long as no one hears.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r6.anchor: على أن الإنصاف هو ترك # الجهر، والعرب تسمي تارك الجهر منصتا وإن كان يقرأ في نفسه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r7.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r7.claim: A Prophetic report exempts al-Fatiha: followers behind him should recite only it, since prayer is not valid without it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r7.anchor: لقوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: "إذا كنتم خلفي فلا تقرءوا إلا بفاتحة الكتاب فإنه لا صلاة إلا بها"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r8.claim: The follower therefore listens to the imam except when reciting al-Fatiha.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r8.anchor: فالمأموم ينصت إلا عن الفاتحة. للخبر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r9.claim: Abu Ishaq allows فاستمعوا له to mean act on its contents and وأنصتوا to mean do not go beyond it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r9.anchor: بما ذكره أبو إسحاق، وهو أنه قال: (يجوز أن يكون: {فاستمعوا له} (¬1) اعملوا بما فيه، {وأنصتوا} لا تجاوزه إلى غيره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r10.claim: On Abu Ishaq's interpretation, the verse says nothing about abandoning recitation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p566/r10.anchor: وعلى هذا فلا معنى لترك القراءة في الآية وليست الآية من ترك القراءة في شيء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p569/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p569/r1.speaker: أهل الظاهر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p569/r1.claim: Some literalists generalize the command and require silence whenever Quran is recited, including for passersby and children's teachers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p569/r1.anchor: وذهب قوم من أهل الظاهر (¬3) إلى أن هذه الآية عامة، ويجب الإنصاف لقارئ الطريق، ومعلم الصبيان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p569/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p569/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p569/r2.claim: The author rejects that broad ruling: obligatory silence applies in prayer and at Friday sermons.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p569/r2.anchor: وليس الأمر على (¬4) ما ذهبوا إليه؛ فإن هذا الإنصات إنما يجب في الصلاة، وعند الخطبة يوم الجمعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p569/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p569/r3.speaker: عبيد بن عمير وعطاء بن أبي رباح
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p569/r3.claim: Al-Jariri reports through Talha ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Kurayz that these two spoke while a storyteller preached; they said the listening command applies in prayer, then resumed talking.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p569/r3.anchor: يدل على هذا ما روى الجريري (¬2) عن طلحة بن عبيد الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r3.claim: The verse was revealed to prohibit speech in prayer, where people had spoken at the beginning.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r3.anchor: نزلت في تحريم الكلام في الصلاة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r4.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r4.claim: Another reported occasion is not reciting aloud behind the imam.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r4.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في ترك الجهر بالقراءة وراء الإمام.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r5.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r5.claim: A further reported occasion is keeping silent for the sermon.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r6.claim: Silence can mean avoiding forbidden speech in prayer, not raising one's voice behind the imam, or quieting to hear the sermon.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:203-205/r6.anchor: وقوله: { وأنصتوا } أي: عما يحرم من الكلام في الصلاة، أو عن رفع الصوت خلف الإمام، أو اسكتوا لاستماع الخطبة.

ELMALILI:7:200-205/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r10.claim: The command to listen and be silent applies when Quran is recited in prayer, a sermon, or any gathering.
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r10.anchor: Kur’an kıraat edildiği vakit namazda veya hutbede veya herhangi mecliste

ELMALILI:7:200-205/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r11.claim: Silence enables attentive listening, which brings insight, faith, and action; faith and action lead to divine mercy and blessing.
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r11.anchor: susmak iyi dinlemeye, iyi dinlemek basirete, basiret iman ve amele, iman ve amel de rahmet ve ni‘met-i ilâhiyeye sebep ve tarîktir

ELMALILI:7:200-205/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r12.claim: Qira'a is a voluntary human act: an intentional sound made by a rational speaker through specific articulation points, joined to intention and understanding.
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r12.anchor: Kıraat ise bir lisan fi‘l-i ihtiyârîsidir ki âkil ve nâtık bir insanın ağzından mehâric-i mahsûsaya itimad ile çıkan

ELMALILI:7:200-205/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r13.claim: Gabriel performs iqra, making the Quran recited, rather than qira'a himself; God's act is revelation and the creation of recitation.
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r13.anchor: Cibrîl’in fiili bile kıraat değil bir ikrâ, yani kıraat ettirmektir

ELMALILI:7:200-205/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r14.claim: An echo or reflected sound is not Quran recitation, so recitation rules such as the prostration of recitation do not follow from it; silent reading is not recitation either.
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r14.anchor: fukahâ bir kıraatin aksinden hâsıl olan sadâ-yı mün‘akise kıraat ve tilâvet hükmü terettüb etmeyeceğini ve meselâ secde-i tilâvet lâzım gelmeyeceğini beyan etmişlerdir

ELMALILI:7:200-205/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r15.claim: A gramophone or radio replay is only the reflected trace of a recitation, not a recitation itself, so the specific duty to listen and be silent does not attach to it.
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r15.anchor: bir kıraat değil, bir kıraatin aksi ve tayfıdır

ELMALILI:7:200-205/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r16.claim: That replay need not be heard as an obligatory or recommended recitation does not make listening impermissible or make refusal obligatory; playing Quran as an instrument is improper.
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r16.anchor: Kur’ân’ı çalmak, çalgılar meyanına koymak şâyân-ı tecviz olmayan bir fiil bulunduğu zâhirdir

ELMALILI:7:200-205/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r17.claim: If Quran is actually recited in an unsuitable place such as a bathhouse, the reader sins, but the listener must still listen; failing to listen is blameworthy.
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r17.anchor: hamamda Kur’an kıraat eden günaha girer, bununla beraber okunduğu takdirde dinlememek de sevab değildir

ELMALILI:7:200-205/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r18.claim: A recording is at least a doubtful trace of recitation because it signifies inner speech; listening is permissible and preferable, disrespect is forbidden, and one should move Quran from an unworthy place.
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r18.anchor: Zira bir kıraat değilse de bir şübhe-i kıraattir. Çünkü kelâm-ı nefsîye dâldir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r1.claim: The verse teaches respectful attention when Quran is recited because it is God’s speech; indifference to it is discourtesy toward God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r1.anchor: Kur’an okunduğu sırada müslüman ona ilgisiz kalmayacak, kulak verip dikkat kesilecek, saygıyla ve ilgiyle dinleyecektir; çünkü o, her şeyden önce Allah’ın sözüdür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r2.claim: Focused listening enables people to reflect on and understand the meanings and benefit from the Quran’s mercy and blessing.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r2.anchor: anlamları üzerine düşünüp kavrayabilmek ve sonuçta rahmet ve bereketinden yararlanabilmek için de onu yoğun bir dikkatle dinlemek gerekmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r3.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur says the command covers literal listening without talking or distraction and metaphorical listening by obeying commands and avoiding prohibitions.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r3.anchor: İbn Âşûr’un da işaret ettiği gibi (IX, 239) “... onu dinleyin ve sessiz durun” buyruğu, beden kulaklarıyla Kur’an’ı dinlemeyi, tilâvet sırasında konuşmamayı, başka şeylerle ilgilenmemeyi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r4.claim: The author prefers taking the verse to command both literal attentive listening during recitation and metaphorical obedience to its teachings.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r4.anchor: En iyisi, âyetin hem hakiki hem de mecazi anlamda Kur’an’a kulak vermeyi emrettiğini kabul ederek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r5.claim: Listening with the ears earns reward for showing respect, while listening with heart and mind illuminates them, strengthens faith, corrects errors, and increases right understanding, bringing mercy into life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r5.anchor: Müslüman, Kur’an-ı Kerîm’i beden kulağı ile dinlemek, Allah’a ve O’nun kelâmına saygı göstermekle Allah kelâmı karşısında takınmış olduğu bu edepli ve ahlâklı tavrının sevabını kazanacak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r6.claim: The Quran’s mercy should be reflected in life and improve both worldly and afterlife outcomes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r6.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’in –bir önceki âyette işaret edilen– “rahmet” özelliğinin de hayatımıza yansıyacağı, dünyamızı ve âhiretimizi güzelleştireceği

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r7.claim: One should avoid audible recitation in markets, streets, cafes, restaurants, or other settings where people cannot practically stop and listen, and avoid projecting mosque recitation outside absent a necessity such as people praying outdoors.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r7.anchor: Çarşı, pazar, sokak, kahvehane, lokanta gibi uygun olmayan ortamlarda, pratikte Kur’an’ı dinlemenin mümkün olmadığı yerlerde açıktan Kur’an okumak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r8.claim: The Prophet’s opponents urged people to drown out the Quran and were condemned; this verse calls Muslims to do the opposite by listening respectfully and earning divine mercy.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r8.anchor: Hz. Peygamber döneminde inkârcıların elebaşıları halka, “Bu Kur’an’a kulak vermeyin, okunurken gürültü yapın, belki bastırırsınız” (Fussılet 41/26)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r9.speaker: Kurtubî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r9.claim: Qurtubi cites a report that this verse was revealed after Fussilat 41:26 in response to the polytheist leaders’ call described there.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r9.anchor: Kurtubî’nin kaydettiği bir rivayette bu âyet, Fussılet sûresinin anılan âyetinden sonra ve müşrik elebaşılarının orada bildirilen çağrılarına cevap olarak inmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r10.speaker: Hasan-ı Basrî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r10.claim: A view attributed to Hasan al-Basri holds that listening whenever Quran is recited is always obligatory.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r10.anchor: Hasan-ı Basrî’ye dayandırılan bir görüşe göre Kur’an okunduğunda onu dinlemek her zaman farzdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r11.speaker: Mâlikîler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r11.claim: The Malikis regard the verse as recommending attentive listening rather than making it obligatory.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r11.anchor: Mâlikîler ise âyetin farziyet değil tavsiye (nedb) anlamı taşıdığını ileri sürmüşlerdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r12.speaker: âlimlerin çoğunluğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r12.claim: Most scholars make listening obligatory when the Prophet recites and, at other times, only during prayer or a sermon when the imam or preacher recites.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r12.anchor: Ancak âlimlerin çoğunluğu bu âyetin sadece Hz. Peygamber Kur’an okuduğunda onu dinlemeyi ve buna ek olarak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r13.speaker: Hanbelî ve Hanefî âlimleri
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r13.claim: Hanbali and Hanafi scholars use the verse to require congregants not to recite while the imam recites Quran, whether aloud or silently.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:204/r13.anchor: Hanbelî ve Hanefî âlimleri, cemaatla namaz esnasında imam açıktan veya gizli olarak Kur’an okurken cemaatin okumamaları gerektiği yönündeki hükmü bu âyete dayandırmışlardır

NAHHAS:v2p171/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p171/r11.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v2p171/r11.claim: Some restrict the instruction to prayer, others to the sermon; ordinary language makes it apply generally unless evidence specifies a context.
NAHHAS:v2p171/r11.anchor: قال أبو جعفر قد ذكرنا أنه يقال إن هذا في الصلوات وقيل إنه في الخطبة وفي اللغة يجب أن يكون في كل شيء

ITQAN:v1p292/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p292/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p292/r1.claim: It is recommended to listen to Quran recitation and avoid idle talk and conversation while it is being recited.
ITQAN:v1p292/r1.anchor: يسن الاستماع لقراءة القرآن وترك اللغط والحديث بحضور القراءة قال تعالى ﴿ وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا لعلكم ترحمون ﴾

ITQAN:v4p434/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p434/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p434/r1.claim: Works on Quranic properties often rely on righteous people's experience; al-Suyuti starts with hadith, then gathers notable statements from early Muslims and the pious.
ITQAN:v4p434/r1.anchor: أفرده بالتصنيف جماعة منهم التميمي وحجة الإسلام الغزالي ومن المتأخرين اليافعي وغالب ما يذكر في ذلك كان مستنده تجارب الصالحين

ITQAN:v4p434/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p434/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v4p434/r2.claim: Ibn Masud reports the Prophet saying honey and the Quran are the two cures; Ibn Majah and others transmit it.
ITQAN:v4p434/r2.anchor: أخرج ابن ماجه وغيره من حديث ابن مسعود ( عليكم بالشفاءين العسل والقرآن )

ITQAN:v4p434/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p434/r3.speaker: علي
ITQAN:v4p434/r3.claim: Ali reports the saying, the best medicine is the Quran.
ITQAN:v4p434/r3.anchor: وأخرج أيضا من حديث علي ( خير الدواء القرآن )

ITQAN:v4p434/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p434/r4.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
ITQAN:v4p434/r4.claim: It was said, according to Talha ibn Musarrif, that a sick person felt relief when the Quran was recited in their presence.
ITQAN:v4p434/r4.anchor: وأخرج أبو عبيد عن طلحة بن مصرف قال ( كان يقال إذا قرئ القرآن عند المريض وجد لذلك خفة )

ITQAN:v4p434/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p434/r5.speaker: واثلة بن الأسقع
ITQAN:v4p434/r5.claim: Wathila ibn al-Asqa reports that the Prophet advised a man with a sore throat to recite the Quran.
ITQAN:v4p434/r5.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي في الشعب عن واثلة بن الأسقع أن رجلا شكا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وجع حلقه قال ( عليك بقراءة القرآن )

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p228#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p228#2/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p228#2/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra says the verse was revealed because people behind Muhammad raised their voices during prayer.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p228#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة في هذه الآية: {وإذا قرئ القرآن} قال: نزلت في رفع الأصوات وهم خلف رسول الله

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p228#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p228#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p228#2/r2.claim: Qatadah says people spoke during prayer when it was first prescribed, even asking one another how many cycles they had prayed; the verse was revealed in response.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p228#2/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: كانوا يتكلمون في صلاتهم في أول ما فرضت، كان الرجل يجيء فيقول لصاحبه

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p228#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p228#2/r3.speaker: الزهري
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p228#2/r3.claim: Al-Zuhri says the verse was revealed about an Ansari youth who recited along whenever Muhammad recited.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p228#2/r3.anchor: وقال الزهري: نزلت في فتى من الأنصار كان رسول الله عليه الصلاة والسلام كلما قرأ شيئا قرأ هو

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p228#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p228#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p228#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the companions recited aloud behind Muhammad in obligatory prayer and confused him, prompting the verse.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p228#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: إن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قرأ في الصلاة المكتوبة، وقرأ أصحابه وراءه رافعين أصواتهم

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p228#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p228#2/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وعطاء وعمرو بن دينار وجماعة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p228#2/r5.claim: Said ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Ata, Amr ibn Dinar, and others say the verse concerns listening silently to the imam during the Friday sermon.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p228#2/r5.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وعطاء وعمرو بن دينار وجماعة: نزلت في الإنصات للإمام في الخطبة يوم الجمعة

TABATABAI:7:205-206/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r1.claim: The verse’s indication is general, although some say it was revealed about congregational prayer.
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r1.anchor: والآية بحسب دلالتها عامة وإن قيل أنها نزلت في الصلاة جماعة

TABATABAI:7:199-206/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r9.claim: Ibn Mardawayh reports from Ibn Abbas that people recited behind the Prophet in prayer and the listening verse was revealed; other versions say they talked, or identify a young Ansari or another man.
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال صلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقرء خلفه قوم فنزلت { وإذا قرئ القرآن

TABATABAI:7:199-206/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r10.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r10.claim: Al-Majmaʿ reports from Abu Jaʿfar that the verse was revealed concerning congregational prayer behind the imam.
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r10.anchor: وفي المجمع بعد ذكر القول أن الآية نزلت في الصلاة جماعة خلف الإمام قال وروي ذلك عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

TABATABAI:7:199-206/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r11.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r11.claim: Abu Abdillah is reported to say that listening silently to Quran recitation is obligatory both during prayer and outside it; al-Ayyashi transmits this through Zurara, including recitation in one’s presence.
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r11.anchor: وروي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام أنه قال يجب الإنصات للقرآن في الصلاة وغيرها. أقول ورواه العياشي عن زرارة عنه عليه السلام

TABATABAI:7:199-206/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي يعفور
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r12.claim: Asked whether one must listen when Quran is recited while he is praying, Abu Abdillah answered yes, saying listening is obligatory whenever Quran is recited.
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r12.anchor: وفيه عن عبد الله بن أبي يعفور عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال قلت له الرجل يقرء القرآن وأنا في الصلاة هل يجب علي الانصات والاستماع

TABATABAI:7:199-206/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r13.speaker: أبو كهمش
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r13.claim: Al-Ayyashi reports from Abu Kahmash that when Ibn al-Kawwa recited a warning verse behind Ali, the Commander of the Faithful listened silently.
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r13.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن أبي كهمش عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال قرء ابن الكواء خلف أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام

TABATABAI:7:199-206/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r14.claim: Reports requiring silence when someone other than the imam recites are understood as recommending it; the author refers the full legal discussion to jurisprudence.
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r14.anchor: أقول والروايات في غير صورة قراءة الإمام محمولة على الاستحباب وتمام البحث في الفقه

THALABI:v4p321/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p321/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
THALABI:v4p321/r1.claim: After hearing people recite behind the imam, Ibn Masud admonished them to understand and reason, citing God's command to listen and be silent.
THALABI:v4p321/r1.anchor: عن بشير بن جابر قال: صلى ابن مسعود فسمع ناسا يقرءون مع الإمام

THALABI:v4p321/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p321/r2.speaker: عبيد بن عمير وعطاء بن أبي رباح
THALABI:v4p321/r2.claim: When challenged for conversing during recitation, Ubayd ibn Umayr and Ata ibn Abi Rabah said the command applies during prayer.
THALABI:v4p321/r2.anchor: فقالا: إنما ذلك في الصلاة: وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا

THALABI:v4p321/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p321/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v4p321/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the verse was revealed because people raised their voices behind the Prophet in prayer.
THALABI:v4p321/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: نزلت هذه الآية في رفع الأصوات وهم خلف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الصلاة

THALABI:v4p321/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p321/r4.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v4p321/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi says people raised their voices during prayer to hear mention of Paradise and Hell, prompting the verse.
THALABI:v4p321/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: وكانوا يرفعون أصواتهم في الصلاة حتى يسمعون ذكر الجنة والنار

THALABI:v4p321/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p321/r5.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v4p321/r5.claim: Qatada says people initially spoke about their needs during prayer, even asking how many units had been prayed; the verse then came down.
THALABI:v4p321/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة: كانوا يتكلمون في الصلاة بحوائجهم في أول ما فرضت عليهم

THALABI:v4p321/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p321/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p321/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says companions recited aloud behind the Prophet during a quiet obligatory prayer and confused his recitation, occasioning the verse.
THALABI:v4p321/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ في الصلاة المكتومة وقرأ أصحابه وراءه رافعين أصواتهم

THALABI:v4p321/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p321/r7.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
THALABI:v4p321/r7.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib says Meccan polytheists told one another not to listen to the Prophet's Quran but to make noise over it, and this verse answered them.
THALABI:v4p321/r7.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب: كان المشركون يأتون رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا صلى فيقول بعضهم لبعض بمكة

THALABI:v4p321/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p321/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وعطاء وعمرو بن دينار وزيد بن أسلم والقاسم بن يسار وشهر بن حوشب
THALABI:v4p321/r8.claim: These authorities say the command concerns listening silently to the imam's Friday sermon.
THALABI:v4p321/r8.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير، ومجاهد، وعطاء، وعمرو بن دينار، وزيد بن أسلم، والقاسم بن يسار، وشهر بن حوشب: هذا في الخطبة

THALABI:v4p321/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p321/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن المبارك
THALABI:v4p321/r9.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak argues for the Friday application because preachers reciting Quran from the minbar precede it with this verse.
THALABI:v4p321/r9.anchor: قال عبد الله بن المبارك: والدليل على حكم هذه الآية في [الجمعة] إنك لا ترى خطيبا على المنبر

THALABI:v4p321/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p321/r10.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v4p321/r10.claim: Al-Hasan applies the command to obligatory prayer and remembrance of God.
THALABI:v4p321/r10.anchor: قال الحسن: هذا في الصلاة المكتوبة وعند الذكر

THALABI:v4p321/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p321/r11.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء
THALABI:v4p321/r11.claim: Mujahid and Ata say listening is obligatory when someone recites Quran during prayer and when the imam preaches.
THALABI:v4p321/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد وعطاء: وجب الإنصات في اثنين عند الرجل يقرأ القرآن وهو يصلي وعند الإمام وهو يخطب

ITQAN:v3p218#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p218#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p218#2/r2.claim: Imperatives can express recommendation or permission; al-Shafi'i explicitly reads the command to make a slave contract as permissive, as with hunting after pilgrimage rites.
ITQAN:v3p218#2/r2.anchor: والإباحة نحو ﴿ فكاتبوهم ﴾ نص الشافعي على أن الأمر فيه للإباحة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r7.claim: Al-Araf opens by mentioning the revealed Book and closes by instructing listeners to hear the Quran, returning to the same Book.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r7.anchor: فانظر كيف بدأت السورة بذكر الكتاب وختمت به أيضاً.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p242#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p242#2/r9.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p242#2/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ defines inshāt as silence for the purpose of listening.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p242#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p242#2/r10.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p242#2/r10.claim: Naṣata, anṣata, and intaṣata all mean to listen silently.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p242#2/r10.anchor: يقال: نصت وأنصت وانتصت بمعنى واحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p242#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p242#2/r11.speaker: الكميت
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p242#2/r11.claim: Al-Farrāʾ notes that al-Kumayt uses inshāt transitively in poetry; the quoted line is not present in this segment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p242#2/r11.anchor: وقد ورد الإنصات متعديا في شعر الكميت

ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r3.claim: On one reading, listen to the Qurʾān with outward ears and be silent with the inward senses.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r4.claim: The pronoun in “listen to it” may refer instead to God: He is the speaker addressing people through the Qurʾān.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r4.anchor: إذا قريء القرآن فاستمعوا للرب جل شأنه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r5.claim: Mercy may come through true hearing or through the manifestation of the Speaker’s qualities and acts in His speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r5.anchor: بالسمع الحقيقي أو برحمة تجلي المتكلم في كلامه بصفاته وأفعاله

ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r15.speaker: السهروردي
