ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r15.claim: Al-Suhrawardī says abundant Qurʾān recitation synchronized by heart and tongue can similarly displace inner speech and make recitation and prayer easy.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r15.anchor: وقد يحصل ما ذكر بتلاوة القرآن أيضا إذا أكثر التلاوة واجتهد في مواطأة القلب مع اللسان

ALUSI-FULL:v9p157/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p157/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p157/r10.claim: After al-Aʿrāf calls the Qurʾān guidance and mercy and commands listening and remembrance, al-Anfāl describes believers whose faith grows when its verses are recited and who trust God.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r1.speaker: الطبري وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī and others report that at Mecca the Companions talked during obligatory prayer about their needs, called out at verses of mercy or punishment, and asked one another whether they had prayed and how much remained.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r1.anchor: ذكر الطبري وغيره أن سبب هذه الآية هو أن أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كانوا بمكة يتكلمون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r2.claim: The author rejects the view that this verse concerns the sermon because it is Meccan and sermons began only after the Prophet’s migration; he also rejects al-Zahrawī’s report of a young Anṣārī reciting while the Prophet recited.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r2.anchor: وأما قول من قال إنها في الخطبة فضعيف، لأن الآية مكية،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r3.speaker: الزهراوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r3.claim: Al-Zahrawī reports that the occasion was a young Anṣārī reciting during prayer while the Prophet recited; the author groups this report with the weak sermon explanation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r3.anchor: وكذلك ما ذكر الزهراوي أنها نزلت بسبب فتى من الأنصار كان يقرأ في الصلاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r4.claim: Muslims unanimously must stop speaking and listen in prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r4.anchor: فأما الاستماع والإنصات عن الكلام في الصلاة فإجماع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r5.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r5.claim: One group says a follower must refrain from reciting altogether, whether the imam recites aloud or silently.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r5.anchor: فقالت فرقة: يمسك المأموم عن القراءة جملة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r6.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r6.claim: Another group says a follower recites when the imam is silent and refrains when the imam recites aloud.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r6.anchor: وقالت فرقة: يقرأ المأموم إذا أسر الإمام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r7.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r7.claim: A third group says that during loud recitation the follower refrains from the sūra but recites the opening sūra, al-Fātiḥa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r7.anchor: وقالت فرقة: يسمك المأموم في جهر الإمام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r8.claim: The author favors the third position and says sound Prophetic reports support it; he does not fully review disagreements because the verse’s wording does not address recitation behind the imam.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r8.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: ومع هذا القول أحاديث صحاح عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r9.claim: The verse requires silence from speech in prayer; silence during the sermon is established by sunna, while the verse applies if Qurʾān is recited in the sermon. Outside prayer, listening is recommended, but honoring the Qurʾān is obligatory in every state.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r9.anchor: فهذه الآية واجبة الحكم في الصلاة أن ينصت عن الحديث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r11.claim: The closing phrase expresses the human hope of receiving mercy.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r12.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r12.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr says the command to listen includes the days of the two feasts and Friday, as well as the imam’s loud recitation in prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p493#2/r12.anchor: وذكر الطبري عن سعيد بن جبير أنه قال في قوله عز وجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the command may mean to act according to the Qurʾān and not transgress it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p494/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج: ويجوز أن يكون فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا

BURHAN:v1p410/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p410/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p410/r2.claim: Rahmah is written with extended ta in seven places; “near” is masculine in one example, marking the active sense, and the mention of traces likewise signals an effect.
BURHAN:v1p410/r2.anchor: فمن ذلك الرحمة مدت فى سبعة مواضع للعلة المذكورة
